### [1] [AutoIndexer: Flexible-Order Decoding by Training Causal Models on Chains of Edits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12545)
*Shu Ishida,Aliasghar Khani,Tianyu Zhang,Cong Luong,James Seale Smith,Adam Gaier*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: AutoIndexer提出了一种基于自回归Transformer的Chain-of-Edits(CoE)解码机制，通过解耦token的生成顺序与显示顺序，使模型能够通过预测编辑标记和光标位置，在生成过程中灵活地对先前的输出进行插入、替换和删除操作，实现类似文本编辑器的迭代修订能力。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 传统自回归LLM受限于因果顺序，难以处理需要事后修订的任务(如交叉引用、章节编号一致性等)，且无法灵活插入或删除任意位置的token。离散扩散LLM虽然支持任意顺序解码，但仍受限于固定长度输出、无法复用KV缓存、且不支持任意位置的插入删除。该研究旨在为自回归模型赋予类似文本编辑器的就地修订能力。

Method: 核心方法包括：(1) Active Context Refinement：通过marker head预测[EDIT]/[RETURN]标记，cursor head预测编辑起止位置(双头指针网络)，支持插入(s=e)、删除(s<e无替换)、替换(s<e有替换)三种操作；(2) Perturbation Training：通过随机采样编辑操作逆向扰动真值序列，构造目标序列τ=E₀⁻¹∘⋯∘Eₙ₋₁⁻¹(x)，模型自回归学习撤销扰动，类似于离散扩散训练；(3) Chain-of-Edits RoPE：将注意力计算分段处理，支持编辑后位置编码的动态重分配，专用的fused kernel实现FlashAttention-4 varlen的高效计算；(4) Sequence Parser：解析生成序列恢复显示顺序。模型基于Qwen3 8B进行LoRA微调，新增cursor head和marker head。

Result: 在标准LLM基准测试中(MMLU、ARC-Challenge、HellaSwag、GSM8K、MATH500、HumanEval、MBPP等)，AutoIndexer 8B LoRA性能基本匹配Qwen3 8B LoRA基线，并在HumanEval上达到59.2%(无指令)和75.61%(有指令)，显著优于LLaDA 8B和Dream 7B等扩散基线。在编辑能力评估中，模型能以约90%准确率区分干净/污染序列，删除和替换情况下约70%正确定位编辑跨度，53/100的删除和18/100的替换可被精确修复。插入是最困难的任务，仅43%触发编辑，但触发时60%正确定位。

Conclusion: AutoIndexer成功为自回归Transformer赋予了主动上下文编辑和细化能力，通过解耦生成顺序与显示顺序，在不牺牲标准LLM性能的前提下引入了类似文本编辑器的修订功能。该方法特别适用于代码生成、长文写作、数学推导等需要迭代细化的领域，可与Chain-of-Thought和工具调用结合，将中间推理过程作为隐藏edit spans处理。展示了因果Transformer实现持续上下文编辑能力的可行性，为生成系统中规划、自我纠正和就地细化的统一优化目标开辟了道路。

Abstract: Autoregressive decoding is less suited to non-causally ordered data, e.g., cross-references or future dependencies, since their outputs cannot be revised post hoc, unlike iterative human reasoning. Diffusion LLMs partially mitigate this limitation but still cannot flexibly insert or remove arbitrary numbers of tokens from a pre-generated context. We design AutoIndexer as a generative model with a novel training and decoding mechanism that simulates a Chain of Edits, allowing the model to flexibly modify its prior outputs in hindsight via token insertions, substitutions, and deletions. The model learns to predict marker tokens for opening and closing edits, simultaneously moving a cursor to positions in the existing token sequence, analogous to a text editor. Training sequences are obtained by perturbing ground-truth labels with inverse chained edit operations, and the model learns to edit by undoing those inverses. The perturbation training allows AutoIndexer to be robust to erroneous context and adaptable to editing tasks such as code correction. We demonstrate that our method exhibits post-generation context-editing capabilities that most autoregressive and diffusion models lack without compromising performance on standard LLM benchmarks. The code is available at this https URL .

</details>


### [2] [Self-Preservation in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12602)
*Dongkyu Cho,Rumi Chunara,Ali Behrouz*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文研究语言模型在持续学习中的"自我保护"问题，探索模型能否利用自身知识选择保留目标来更广泛地保护其能力。通过构建任务库(Task Banks)并使用冻结模型生成重放数据，作者发现：(1)新任务和学习率决定遗忘模式，平均准确率可能掩盖正确答案的丢失；(2)生成的重放数据可减少任务库之外任务的遗忘，组合部分任务库能增强保护效果；(3)在4B模型上，基于新任务信息的选择优于随机选择。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 持续学习中，预训练模型需要适应新任务同时保留已有能力，但用于保护的任务和数据的限制覆盖范围有限，而遗忘可能超出这些范围。研究模型能否利用自身知识帮助选择保留目标，以更广泛地保护其能力——即"自我保护"问题。

Method: 作者构建任务库(Task Banks)框架：将任务描述和示例组织成条目，可选择并组合以指导冻结模型生成重放数据。在Qwen3系列模型(0.6B/1.7B/4B)上进行指令微调实验，引入"保留率"(Retention)指标衡量原本正确的回答中仍保持正确的比例，并系统比较：(1)新任务与学习率对遗忘的影响；(2)生成式重放vs真实重放vs仅SFT；(3)部分任务库组合的效果；(4)随机选择vs基于任务库选择vs基于新任务感知选择的差异。

Result: 三项核心发现：(1)新任务和学习率影响哪些已有能力退化，追踪原本正确的回答可揭示平均准确率掩盖的损失；(2)生成式重放减少任务库外的遗忘，组合两个部分任务库在三个模型规模上将平均保留率分别提升4.42/3.32/2.99 pp；(4)在4B模型上，新任务感知选择将平均保留率提升至95.69%，超过随机选择(92.94%)和仅任务库选择(93.42%)，但小模型无此优势。固定示例预算下，替换新任务示例为重放数据会以减少新任务增益为代价改善保留。

Conclusion: 语言模型可通过生成重放数据来支持更广泛的自我保护，并在某些设置下帮助选择重放目标。任务 банks提供了一种系统研究部分能力清单下保留问题的框架。生成式重放数据可减少遗忘，组合部分任务库可改善保留率，基于新任务信息的目标选择在4B设置下有优势，但在小模型上未观察到相应优势。研究强调了同时评估保留行为和新任务学习的必要性，因为平均准确率可能掩盖已失去的正确答案。

Abstract: Continual learning (CL) seeks to adapt pretrained models while preserving prior capabilities. Yet the tasks supplied for preservation cover only part of what a model knows, while forgetting can extend beyond them. Recent work shows that language models can supplement this limited evidence by generating useful replay without access to their original training data. This raises a question about self-preservation: can a model help choose preservation targets that protect its own capabilities more broadly? To study this question, we organize task descriptions and their examples into Task Banks, whose entries can be selected and combined to guide replay generation by a frozen model. Continual instruction tuning with Qwen models of varying sizes yields three findings. First, the new task and learning rate shape which prior capabilities degrade, while tracking previously correct answers reveals losses that average accuracy can conceal. Second, generated replay reduces forgetting on tasks outside the bank. Combining partial banks strengthens this protection, improving mean retention of previously correct answers over either bank alone across the tested sizes. Third, the model can also help choose replay targets: selection informed by the new task improves mean held-out retention over random selection at 4B, with similar new-task gains, although smaller models show no corresponding advantage. Under a fixed example budget, however, replacing new-task examples with replay improves preservation at the cost of smaller new-task gains. Together, these findings show that models can support broader self-preservation by generating replay data and, in some settings, choosing which tasks to replay.

</details>


### [3] [GeoFitBench-LLM: A Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Capabilities in Geospatial Data Requirements Elicitation for Geo-Analytic Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12669)
*Amirhossein Vahdat,Thierry Badard,Luc Lamontagne*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: GeoFitBench-LLM is a benchmark evaluating whether LLMs can identify the geospatial datasets, supporting resources, and constraints required by geo-analytic requests in natural language, structured around Spatio-Temporal Relational and Semantic Grounding reasoning dimensions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 随着大语言模型成为GeoAI系统的核心，现有评估很少考察其在地理空间数据需求提取方面的能力。这对于检索型地理分析任务至关重要，因为若无法先确定所需的数据集和约束，相关任务无法可靠执行。

Method: 提出了基于两维度（时空关系推理与语义基础）构建的GeoFitBench-LLM基准，采用固定的、与提供商无关的schema编码真实需求（资源识别与属性级规范），对七个LLM在最小提示下进行资源识别与fitness-for-use规范能力的可复现评估。

Result: 在最小提示下，识别所需资源通常可行；GPT-5.4 Thinking表现最佳，在66.67%的请求中恢复了完整资源集。然而，随着推理需求增加，准确进行fitness-for-use规范仍较为困难。

Conclusion: 当前LLM在识别geo-analytic所需的地理空间资源方面已展现初步能力，但在细致的fitness-for-use属性级规范上仍有显著不足，强调了未来需要在更高复杂度推理方面提升模型能力。

Abstract: Large language models are becoming central to GeoAI systems, yet their evaluation rarely considers the elicitation of geospatial data requirements. This omission is critical as retrieval oriented geo-analytic tasks cannot be supported reliably without first identifying the necessary datasets and constraints. GeoFitBench-LLM is introduced as a benchmark for assessing whether LLMs can infer the datasets, the supporting resources and the constraints required by geo-analytic requests in natural language. The benchmark is structured around two reasoning dimensions, Spatio-Temporal Relational and Semantic Grounding, reflecting long-standing challenges in geospatial information retrieval and related natural language tasks. Ground truth requirements are encoded in a fixed, provider-independent schema for reproducible evaluation of resource identification and attribute-level specification. Experiments on seven models under minimal prompting indicate that identifying the necessary resources is often achievable, with GPT-5.4 Thinking achieving the best result by recovering the complete set of resources in 66.67% of benchmark requests. Results further indicate that accurate fitness-for-use specification remains more difficult as inferential demands increase.

</details>


### [4] [Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707)
*Yueying Li,Jingxuan Fan,Kianté Brantley,Sham M. Kakade,Hanlin Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出了一种无需人工偏好标注的多模态奖励建模方法：在冻结的Qwen3-VL骨干网络中间层上训练一个仅含约2000参数的线性头，利用同图字幕扰动作为无需标注的负样本。在32B规模上以约千分之一的微调算力，在三个奖励基准上达到或超过GPT-4o（包括VL-RewardBench上领先6.6分）。研究还发现奖励基准排名无法预测Best-of-N部署效果，并提出用策略自身错误通过验证器自举来改进部署。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有视觉-语言奖励模型依赖昂贵且存在标注分歧的人工偏好对，并以基准准确率排名。这带来两个问题：(1) 标注成本高且不一致；(2) 基准排名是否真正反映实际部署性能存疑。论文核心探讨：奖励模型学到了什么，以及基准分数何时停止预测部署表现。

Method: 核心方法包含四个组件：
1. **中间层探针**：在冻结的Qwen3-VL骨干的中间层（如2B取N-4层，32B取N-12层）上附加一个无偏置的线性头，仅训练约2048个参数。
2. **扰动采样器（无标注监督）**：通过一组扰动算子 T_near（属性替换）、T_splice（拼接）、T_shuf（重排）、T_×（跨图）对同一图的正例字幕进行编辑生成负样本，保持作者、长度、风格一致；图像响应则对提示做扰动并用同种子渲染对比。
3. **训练目标**：矩阵版 Bradley-Terry损失（in-batch，每个正例对8个负样本）。
4. **验证器驱动自举**：用策略自身Best-of-N候选取由廉价验证器标注，重新训练头部用于部署。
理论分析上将目标解释为噪声对比估计（NCE）的排序版本，证明凸性，并由采样器对分布定义奖励方向。

Result: 主要实验结果：
- 32B探针在三个基准上达到或匹配GPT-4o：Multimodal RewardBench总体.733、VL-RewardBench总体.724（领先GPT-4o .658约6.6分）、MMRB2推理.742。
- 中间层选择贡献5.8分，超过最末层。
- 在相同样本对预算下，扰动挖掘的负样本比RLAIF-V精选对多教会冻结头3-5分。
- 两个在同一扰动数据上训练的头在基准上打平，但在幻觉判断上差6.4分，证明采样器而非分数定义奖励。
- 在2B/8B生成器上重新训练头于验证器标注的自生成候选，使COCO字幕CHAIR幻觉降低5.1分，图像生成Best-of-12通过率提升5.4分；但对应头在所有奖励基准上得分更低。
- Best-of-N中，基准排名与部署价值无单调关系；当多数投票可信度低时，训练好的探针与训练免费的log-likelihood评判相当。
- DPO在自生成对上演示可降低幻觉3-6个CHAIR点，QA无代价。

Conclusion: 冻结的视觉-语言表征配合中间层探针和同图字幕扰动，可用千分之一的算力实现强大的多模态奖励建模。探针深度与训练比较的分布共同决定头部学习到的信号。相似基准得分可隐藏不同专长，更高的偏好准确率未必带来更好的Best-of-N选择。从策略自身错误出发的验证器监督可改进候选排序但降低基准准确率——真正帮助部署的监督来自策略自己的错误。因此，选用奖励模型时应测试其在策略自身样本上的最佳选择能力，论文报告时应说明训练所用的比较分布。方法局限：仅覆盖两个骨干家族，CHAIR指标同时充当训练标签与评估指标，最佳基准表现与最佳部署表现的统一仍未解决。

Abstract: Vision-language reward models are trained on annotated preference pairs, which are expensive to collect, can disagree, and are ranked by benchmark accuracy. We build one with no human preference label: a linear head on an intermediate layer of a frozen Qwen3-VL backbone, trained to score a web caption above a perturbed version of the same caption; labeled data enters only to select the layer. The layer is the decisive choice, worth 5.8 points over the last layer, and one recipe transferred without re-tuning beats or at least matches GPT-4o on three benchmarks at 32B, 6.6 points ahead on VL-RewardBench, from a few thousand parameters at about a thousandth of fine-tuning compute. At an equal pair budget, perturbations teach a frozen head 3 to 5 points more than curated RLAIF-V pairs. Because the backbone is frozen, the objective is convex, and the perturbation sampler specifies the reward, which the benchmark does not identify: two heads trained on disjoint halves of the same perturbations tie on the benchmark and differ by 6.4 points in hallucination judging. Retraining the head on the policy's own verifier-labeled candidates cuts caption hallucination by 5.1 CHAIR points and lifts image-generation pass rate by 5.4, while scoring lower on every reward benchmark. Together, an intermediate-layer probe, free same-image perturbations, and a verifier-driven bootstrap turn give a recipe for multimodal reward modeling that needs no annotator, costs a fraction of fine-tuning, and is specified by the comparisons it is trained on rather than by a benchmark rank.

</details>


### [5] [COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12837)
*Kavinda Kehelella,Sanghamitra Dutta*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出COFFEQA，一种针对开放书问答的少样本知识蒸馏方法，通过利用反事实样本为决策边界附近的事实样本提供额外监督，并引入上下文跟随难度（CFD）指标验证反事实质量，在多个QA基准上显著优于仅基于事实的蒸馏基线。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 传统知识蒸馏需要大量数据和计算资源，尤其在生成式任务中成本高昂。少样本蒸馏虽能减少数据需求，但其性能严重依赖于训练样本的选择。研究发现，靠近教师决策边界的不确定样本会显著降低蒸馏性能，因此需要一种数据高效的方法来应对这一挑战。

Method: 1) 定义生成式QA中的反事实为最小修改的上下文，使其诱导教师模型产生替代答案；2) 通过GPT-4o-mini三阶段生成反事实（实体类型分类、生成替代实体、最小修改上下文）；3) 提出Context Following Difficulty (CFD) 指标，结合Answer Agreement (AA) 和 Contextual Loss Ratio (CLR) 验证反事实；4) 提供几何分析，使用Hausdorff距离刻画教师-学生决策边界偏差，证明d_H ≤ α + ε；5) 在相同少样本预算下，用k/2个边界附近事实样本配对k/2个反事实样本进行蒸馏。

Result: 在T5和Qwen2.5两个模型族、五个领域内（NQ、SQuAD、NewsQA、TriviaQA、HotpotQA）和三个领域外（D、DuoRC、RelationExtraction）QA基准上的实验表明：COFFEQA在所有三种蒸馏基线（KD、LWD、SeqKD）下均优于仅基于事实的蒸馏。例如，在T5设置下使用32个少样本对时，TriviaQA上平均EM提升8.77分，F1提升9.98分。方法还提升了教师-学生一致性，并在修改上下文证据的测试中表现更佳。消融实验证实CFD验证的有效性。

Conclusion: COFFEQA证明了反事实引导的少样本蒸馏在生成式开放书QA中的有效性，通过为决策边界附近的事实样本提供反事实监督，能够在有限监督下更高效地传递教师知识。几何分析为理解反事实如何约束师生边界对齐提供了理论依据，CFD指标确保了反事实质量。局限性在于当前仅适用于基于实体的答案类型和开放书QA任务，未来可扩展到更广泛的答案类型和生成式任务。

Abstract: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model for resource-constrained environments. However, the process of distillation is typically data-intensive and computationally expensive, particularly for generative tasks. Few-shot distillation offers an alternative by transferring teacher knowledge using limited training samples. However, we observe that few-shot distillation performance is heavily dependent on the choice of these training samples. In fact, we demonstrate that using more uncertain samples near the teacher's decision boundary can significantly deteriorate distillation performance. Motivated by this observation, we propose Counterfactual-guided Few-shot Distillation in Open-book Question Answering (COFFEQA), a novel strategy that aptly uses counterfactuals to provide additional supervision around challenging factual samples. In the generative QA setting, we define a counterfactual as a minimally modified context that induces the teacher to change its response to an alternative answer. We provide geometric insights on how factual-counterfactual pairs can constrain the deviation between the teacher's and student's decision boundaries. We further introduce a new metric, Context Following Difficulty (CFD) that further validates counterfactuals prior to distillation based on agreement with the intended alternative answer and dependence on the modified context. COFFEQA uses CFD-validated factual-counterfactual pairs for few-shot distillation. Experiments across five in-domain and three out-of-domain QA benchmarks using T5 and Qwen2.5 families show that COFFEQA outperforms factual-only distillation baselines under the same few-shot budget. For instance, on TriviaQA, COFFEQA improves over the factual-only baseline by 8.77 average EM points and 9.98 average F1 points under the T5 setting with 32 few-shot pairs.

</details>


### [6] [Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12939)
*Raghavv Goel,Sudhanshu Agrawal,Mukul Gagrani,Risheek Garrepalli,Mingu Lee*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出了一个基于矩阵熵和中心核对齐（CKA）的原则性框架，用于推测解码（speculative decoding）中的多层隐藏状态选择，通过信息量和多样性两个互补准则优化层选择策略。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有推测解码方法通常依赖基于位置的固定启发式规则（如 EAGLE3 的 [2, N//2, N-3]）来选择目标模型的层子集，而最优层子集的选择本质上是一个组合问题，即使对中等深度模型进行穷举评估也不可行。需要一个原则性框架来指导层选择。

Abstract: Counterfactual text editing is the ability to revise a given text in light of a hypothetical change while preserving facts not causally affected by that change. This requires causal understanding: a model must determine, without being explicitly instructed to, what events are affected by the hypothetical change and what should remain fixed. This skill is central to human reasoning, especially in safety-critical domains like healthcare or law.   <summary>Details</summary>

Method: 在黑盒设置下，利用beam搜索的top-k候选集，通过候选AMR图之间的成对相似性矩阵估计不确定性。具体使用四种UE方法：(1) LexSim基于ROUGE-L的词汇相似性；(2) DegMat基于归一化总边权；(3) EigV基于归一化Laplacian的特征值偏差；(4) Ecc基于Laplacian特征空间中候选嵌入的离心率。相似性函数包括Smatch、S²Match、SEMA和WLK。预测质量通过Smatch++、S²Match和SemBLEU衡量。可靠性通过Prediction Rejection Ratio (PRR)评估，将按不确定性排序后逐步拒绝的剩余预测平均质量曲线下面积相对于随机基线和oracle进行归一化。实验在AMR 3.0测试集（n=1898）上对6个解析器（SPRING、IBM-Parser、MBSE、HMG-AMR-BART、HMG-AMR-T5、IBM-Neural）展开，beam大小k∈{3,5,8,10}。

  <summary>Details</summary>

  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有自纠错方法通常需要微调整个LLM或训练外部评论家/验证器，成本高昂；而内联反射令牌注入在固定生成预算下难以可靠地重新引导推理轨迹。需要一种轻量级、训练代价低的方法来识别失败轨迹中的干预位置并以更有效的方式重定向。

Method: UPTURN包含三部分：（1）位置策略——130K参数MLP头作用于冻结的Qwen3-0.6B编码器，在段落边界（\n\n）处打分候选截断位置，使用基于GRPO的组内优势估计（对同一失败轨迹的多个截断位置采样并比较再生成功率）进行训练；（2）门控器——66K参数MLP，从\boxed{}令牌处的隐藏状态预测正确性，用于推理时筛选需纠错的rollout；（3）多轮注入——关闭当前助手轮，将固定指令（"Resolve this concisely."）作为新用户轮注入，开启新的助手轮重新生成，且前缀+后缀总长不超过原响应预算。训练时奖励来自再生后缀的正确率均值，无需逐步标注或LLM微调。

Result: 在四个推理器（Qwen3-4B/8B、DeepSeek-R1-Qwen3-8B、QwQ-32B）和六个数学基准上，UPTURN@16相比Base@32在每个基准和模型上均提升平均准确率（37.1%→55.3%），pass rate除一项外全部提升；在L_max预算下比Reflexion高+16.2平均准确率/15.9 pass率，超过AlphaOne、CyclicReflex等内联注入基线；在2L_max预算下仍保持+4.9/+0.8优势；位置策略可跨模型迁移且不重训即可提升GPQA-Diamond；与Reflexion/SCoRe/GRPO互补，叠加后仍获得额外提升；种子鲁棒性良好（标准差约2点）；即使使用地面真值门控器，相比学习门控仅改善≤0.6点。

Conclusion: 结构（用户轮转换边界）比指令内容更重要：将指令置于新用户轮中能可靠重定向推理，而内联注入会被吸收为模型自身的延续；通过学习截断位置并以多轮方式注入，可避免昂贵的LLM微调；当所需能力已具备时，轻量级学习干预即可恢复更好的推理路径。代码扩展到代码与工具使用领域仍是开放问题。

Abstract: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it retains a selected prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline. It outperforms self-correction and reflection-token injection baselines under matched correction budgets, transfers across reasoners and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining, and complements GRPO and self-correction methods.

</details>


### [12] [Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13895)
*Sovesh Mohapatra,Dani S Bassett*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 该论文研究了大型语言模型中共享注意力头在不同任务下的功能变化。受网络神经科学启发，作者提出了一种"网络视角"来理解语言模型计算：通过比较固定模型组件在不同任务中的行为，证明了相同的注意力头会根据任务上下文改变其响应的事实以及组件间的交互方式。在五个开源模型（Gemma-2-9B、Qwen3-14B、Llama-3.1-8B、Falcon-H1-1.5B/7B）上进行了实验，发现：（1）影响力（下游响应）随任务变化而重新分配；（2）任务上下文改变头部对事实的响应及对后续组件的影响；（3）任务特定的线性响应图比平均响应图更准确地预测下游反应（Gemma降低53.6%，Qwen降低5.0%的均方误差）。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 大型语言模型能在单一参数集下执行多种任务，但相同的注意力头跨任务被复用。现有研究虽能识别共享头，但未能解释这些共享头在不同任务中扮演的不同角色。受网络神经科学关于任务依赖性脑区交互研究的启发，作者希望以网络视角理解语言模型中的计算机制。核心问题：当图事实固定时，改变任务是否会改变相同组件响应的事实以及它们输出对后续组件的影响？

Method: 论文采用基于图任务的实验范式。**任务设计**：使用三边有向图（A→B, B→C, A→C），比较"Compose path"（检查路径）和"Read direct edge"（检查直接边）两种任务，共享相同图事实。**测量方法**：(1) 影响力（Influence）——通过在源头施加±2δ扰动，量化对下游接收者的影响；(2) 重要性（Importance）——替换激活向量后正确答案logit边际的下降。**内部任务编辑**：使用对比激活加法，在不改写指令的情况下切换模型读取的事实。**线性响应映射**：通过源头扰动构建预测下游头部响应的线性映射，分别在编辑前后估计。**控制设计**：使用维度置换和符号翻转的源/下游控制值以排除非特异性效应。**模型**：5个1.5B-14B参数的开源模型。

Result: 主要结果包括：(1) **影响力随任务重新分布**：在Falcon-H1-1.5B中，H1对H2的影响力从-0.0145（Compose path）变为0.00101（Read direct edge）；H1对H3的影响力从0.0107翻倍至0.0238。六维影响力比例的角度变化比四维重要性比例更大（Gemma: 30.17° vs 较小；Qwen: 11.98°）。(2) **任务选择性事实效应**：在Gemma中，三个边的事实干预产生13-17 logits的任务选择性差异；Qwen产生36-52 logits差异。(3) **内部任务编辑重定向事实响应**：在Gemma-2-9B和Qwen3-14B中，早期激活编辑使模型在512个反向答案提示上100%切换答案；Fact 2在H2和H3的响应份额分别增加78.9和97.1个百分点（Gemma），Qwen中为68.7和91.8个百分点。(4) **任务上下文改善预测**：任务特定映射将均方预测误差降低53.6%（Gemma）和5.0%（Qwen）相比平均映射。(5) **相关性加强响应**：在AND任务下，相同H2位移在相关上下文产生比不相关上下文大1.40倍（Gemma）和1.53倍（Qwen）的H3响应。

Conclusion: 该论文证明：共享组件能同时改变其响应的事实和影响后续计算的方式。影响力和答案重要性提供了组件角色的互补描述，因为它们的相对模式在任务间以不同程度变化。在Gemma和Qwen中，早期激活编辑在书面指令保持固定的情况下转移了事实响应和影响力。因此测量的角色取决于模型的内部任务状态。这种依赖性对预测也很重要：在同一提示内，与当前状态匹配的响应图更准确地预测下游事实效应。这些发现表明网络视角可能有助于解释模型如何使用共享参数执行不同计算；任务依赖性影响力的测量也可能指导旨在改变一种行为同时保留其他行为的干预措施。未来方向包括测试影响力测量是否能预测提示外的响应、使用稀疏特征电路追踪可解释特征间的因果交互、以及在更长文本中检验上下文依赖性相关工作。

Abstract: Large language models reuse the same attention heads across tasks, but identifying these shared heads does not explain what they do differently in each task. A natural source of inspiration is task-dependent interactions among shared brain regions, which motivate a network view of language-model computation. Here, we compare fixed model components across tasks using identical graph facts, statements specifying which directed connections are present. We measure how interventions affect attention heads and the activation state in later layers (influence), as well as the answer (importance). Task changes redistribute the influence in five open-weight models spanning four families and 1.5-14 billion parameters. In Gemma-2-9B and Qwen3-14B, an activation edit changes an early internal activation vector and switches which fact the model reads while the written instruction stays fixed. The same heads then respond to different graph facts and influence later components differently. For each prompt, we construct two linear response maps, one before the edit and one after it. Each map predicts a later head's response from a measured change in an earlier head. For a separate factual intervention, the map for the corresponding condition reduces mean squared prediction error by 53.6% in Gemma and 5.0% in Qwen compared with the average of the two maps. These findings show that task context changes both which graph facts the shared components respond to and how their outputs affect later computation. A network account may help explain how models use shared parameters to perform different computations. Measurements of task-dependent influence could also guide interventions intended to alter one behavior while preserving others.

</details>


### [13] [SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12569)
*Wei Minn,Zhensu Sun,Lwin Khin Shar,David Lo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: SWE-Duel 提出了一种自扩展的编码智能体竞技场，通过红蓝对抗回合让两个编码智能体互相出题和评测，任务和判据在评估时实时生成，难度由参与者决定而非固定，从而避免数据污染和饱和问题。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有静态编码基准存在两个根本缺陷：(1) 任务在发布后逐渐泄露到训练数据中；(2) 任务难度固定，更强的智能体最终会将其饱和。需要一种"自扩展"基准，其任务与判据在评估时动态生成，难度由参与者决定。

Method: 红蓝对抗竞技场：Red 智能体在真实代码库上分三个上下文隔离会话（功能实现、缺陷嵌入、盲自修复）生成新功能并植入隐藏缺陷；通过三个验证门控确保缺陷可验证且可修复。Blue 智能体在不知情的情况下审查 PR，需同时通过已有测试、功能测试和密封的缺陷测试才能获胜。每位参与者轮流担任红蓝两角色，通过 Bradley-Terry 评分进行排名。

Result: 在 11 个模型-框架组合、15 个代码库、1500 回合的竞赛中：GPT-5.5 + Codex CLI 以 98.3% 的缺陷修复率成为最强解题者；Claude Opus 4.8 + mini-swe-agent 以 27.3% 的 Red 胜率成为最强出题者。GLM 模型家族的版本递增实验中，新版本任务击败固定参考解题者的比例（42.9%）远高于旧版本（4.0%），初步证明任务难度随出题能力提升而扩展。

Conclusion: SWE-Duel 实现了自扩展编码基准，任务在评估时生成避免泄露，难度由参与者能力决定可随进步提升。1,500 回合竞赛展示了不同智能体在出题与解题能力上的差异化表现，为编码智能体评估提供了一个可持续、抗污染的新框架。同时该系统具有双用途风险，需谨慎管理。

Abstract: Static coding benchmarks are fixed at release. Over time their tasks leak into training data, and stronger agents eventually saturate them. We argue that a benchmark should instead aim to be self-scaling: its tasks and oracles are created at evaluation time, so no content exists in advance to leak, and its difficulty is set by the participating agents rather than fixed at release. We introduce SWE-Duel, an arena in which two coding agents evaluate each other over mirrored Red-Blue turns. In each turn, the Red agent works on a real repository across three context-isolated sessions. It proposes and implements a new feature with feature tests, then embeds a subtle bug in that feature along with sealed bug-triggering tests. The resulting pull request is admitted only if (1) it passes the feature tests and the repository's existing tests while failing exactly the bug tests, and (2) a fresh session of the same agent can repair the bug blind, which rules out unsolvable tasks. The Blue agent then reviews the pull request without being told a bug exists. It wins only if its revision passes all three test suites, and then the two agents swap roles. We run a tournament among 11 model-harness participants on 15 repositories in five languages for 1,500 turns. The leaders win in different ways. GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI ranks first as the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviews. Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent ranks second as the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate. Finally, within one model family, tasks written by the newest version defeat a fixed-reference solver far more often than those of older versions (42.9% vs. 4.0%), giving preliminary evidence that task difficulty scales with task authoring capability.

</details>


### [14] [Rethinking the Roles of Diffusion and Decoding: Predictive-State Flows for Parallel Language Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12898)
*Jinjin He,Xinsong Feng,Lucheng Fu,Sinan Wang,Bo Zhu,Jiayun Wang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: In continuous diffusion language models (DLMs), latents generated by the diffusion prior are mapped almost deterministically to tokens, either by a decoder or through a token embedding matrix. Unlike in image generation, where visual details can vary continuously, the diffusion prior must capture fine-grained discrete token choices in continuous space, which can make the joint latent distribution difficult to model. We argue that generative roles should instead be divided: the diffusion prior should generate high-level predictive information, while the decoder should resolve the remaining token-level choices. Based on this view, we introduce Predictive-State Flows (PSF), which partitions a sequence into blocks and associates each block with a predictive state computed solely from the preceding context. A rectified-flow prior generates the sequence of predictive states, after which a block-causal decoder generates all blocks in parallel, autoregressively only within each block. This design reduces diffusion from L token-level states to K << L predictive states and reduces token-level sequential depth to L/K. On unconditional OpenWebText generation, a 197M-parameter model with K=8 achieves a generative perplexity of 22.8 at entropy 5.16 using 0.31 TFLOPs per 1024-token document, versus 24.0 and 7.2 TFLOPs for ELF-B with 32 sampling steps. The corresponding measured operating points yield MAUVE@512 of 0.93 and 0.73, respectively. Controlled comparisons further show that content states, which additionally encode their own blocks, yield 8-16% higher generative perplexity than predictive states, and that replacing sampled predictive-state trajectories with a shared mean lowers MAUVE@512 by 0.11. These results suggest that latent design for continuous DLMs should consider not only how compactly text is represented, but also how generative roles are divided between the prior and the decoder.

### [15] [Forecasting Corpus-Sampling Disagreement in Masked Text Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12987)
*Hare Krishna*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: If a second text corpus were collected from the same population, how much would a predictor's outputs change? We study this question for masked-text reconstruction using a smoothed predictor built from nearby token-pair counts and evaluated over the full 50,257-token GPT-2 vocabulary. Treating each source document as one observation, we derive a first-order formula for the expected disagreement between predictors fitted to two independent corpora. The formula accounts for variable document length, random context counts, and correlations across token offsets, and it can be evaluated from a separate reference corpus without access to either target corpus. On TinyStories, WikiText-103, and CNN/DailyMail, growing each corpus from 512 to 2,048 chunks of 64 tokens lowers disagreement by only 5--40\%, far short of the 75\% implied by $1/n$ scaling. The forecast tracks this slow decline, which we trace to smoothing of rarely seen contexts. Forecast accuracy depends less on how these correlations are modeled than on the size of the reference corpus: small references systematically underpredict disagreement. A source-split jackknife that uses only reference data reduces this calibration error by 57--59\%. After this correction, a simpler smoothed-multinomial approximation is most accurate when the reference corpus is smaller than the target corpus, and a nonlinear source bootstrap is most accurate when it is larger. Finally, small masked diffusion language models trained on the same corpora show that the count-based forecasts partly identify which inputs are most sensitive to the corpus, but miss the neural models' much faster decline in disagreement.

### [16] [Neurograf v1: An End-to-End Romanian-First Language Model Family](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13134)
*Ionut Adrian Rotaru*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We present Neurograf v1, an experimental end-to-end Romanian-first language-model pipeline developed to investigate the feasibility of training language models from scratch for a lower-resource European language. The pipeline comprises RoSfera, a 635 GB Romanian corpus containing 175.7 million documents; an 80k byte-level BPE tokenizer; five decoder-only models ranging from 160M to 6B parameters, trained on 131 billion tokens; three instruction-tuned assistants; and two contrastively trained embedding models. Training and evaluation were conducted using computing infrastructure at ELI-NP/IFIN-HH. The model family exhibits consistent scaling of validation loss and increasing Romanian factual and cultural knowledge with model size. On the 1,000-question WWTBM benchmark, Neurograf-6B achieves 69.89% accuracy on Romanian-context questions, while Neurograf-3.2B reaches 67.38%. Compute-optimal analysis yields a parameter-scaling exponent of approximately 0.423. Neurograf v1 serves as an experimental demonstrator rather than a production system. The study identifies practical challenges involving diacritic preservation, corpus quality, data composition, and tokenization efficiency, while demonstrating the feasibility of developing Romanian-first base models, instruction-following assistants, and semantic embedding models within a unified training pipeline.

### [17] [Do Prompt Optimizers Break Requirements They Are Not Scored On? A Preregistered Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13287)
*Sangdo Han,Moonsoo Kim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Prompt optimizers rewrite a prompt to raise one target metric, but prompts also state requirements the metric does not score, such as an output format, citations, or abstention. In a preregistered study, we run GEPA, MIPROv2, and TextGrad on HotpotQA, SQuAD 2.0, and IFEval and count per-item violations of unscored requirements with deterministic checks. By the preregistered criterion, all three optimizers produce regressions, substantially on HotpotQA, where net regression in citation validity reaches 10.7 to 41.6 points while exact match rises by 21 to 34 points. A post-hoc decomposition changes this reading. The optimized prompts elicit reasoning before the required JSON object, and under the 200-token output cap used throughout, 13.9% to 47.0% of responses end before any answer appears. Among parseable outputs, net regression is within 3 points of zero. With a 1,024-token cap, extraction failures disappear, content regression stays below 1 point, and exact match rises further. Two simple gates fail the preregistered criterion. The side effect is narrower than hypothesized: optimized prompts are more accurate and break an explicit output contract, and a lenient target metric does not show the cost.

### [18] [Overcoming Data Imbalances with Expert Selection Biases](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13370)
*Ayush K. Tarun,Clara Meister,Antoine Bosselut*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have become the standard architecture for frontier LLMs. The multiple parallel experts in each transformer block theoretically enable expert specialization according to categories such as domains, languages, or modalities during pretraining. However, when data is imbalanced across categories, minority categories can become concentrated in a small fraction of the expert pool or spread inefficiently across them, effectively limiting their available capacity. In this work, we demonstrate that category-conditioned expert-selection biases can preferentially route tokens from different categories toward specialized expert pools. By applying biases based on input category, we provide a simple way to induce soft category-aligned specialization. This intervention encourages categories toward distinct expert subsets while retaining cross-category sharing when useful. More importantly, it enables the over-allocation of expert capacity to categories that would otherwise be disadvantaged by data scarcity. We observe performance improvements across modalities, low-resource languages, and code in models up to 10.6B parameters. At our smallest and largest model scales, these gains are equivalent to allocating 18.5% and 2.7% additional baseline training tokens, respectively. Overall, our results show that expert biases can serve as a lightweight control for category-level expert allocation, making room for low-resource categories while retaining standard MoE inference.

### [19] [Contextual Correction of Parallel Draftsfor Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12570)
*Roy Eisenstadt,Harel Lidar,Tal Gonen,Omer Luxembourg,Itamar Zimerman,Lior Wolf,Eli David,Ilan Naiman*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a lightweight drafter to propose multiple tokens that are subsequently verified in parallel by the target model. Recent diffusion-based drafters make this paradigm particularly attractive: deep attention-based neural backbones provide strong predictions, while drafting multiple future positions in parallel avoids the sequential cost of autoregressive generation. This parallelism, however, comes at a cost. Tokens within a draft block are predicted without access to the realized identities of preceding draft tokens, removing intra-block dependencies that would naturally be available under autoregressive generation. We introduce DCOCO (DFlash Contextual Corrector), a lightweight mechanism that restores these dependencies while preserving parallel drafting. Rather than committing to each position's top prediction, DCOCO retains multiple candidate tokens and evaluates their contextual compatibility across adjacent draft positions in parallel, enabling contextually informed token selection at low additional cost. Across four verifier backbones and ten benchmarks, DCOCO achieves the highest average throughput in every evaluated configuration, spanning greedy and stochastic decoding with and without extended reasoning, with speedups of up to 6.6x over vanilla decoding. Its advantage persists under concurrent serving: DCOCO outperforms the strongest competing method by 6-23% across 4-32 concurrent requests, while other sequential correctors fall below uncorrected DFlash at these loads. These results demonstrate that recovering intra-block dependencies through parallel contextual scoring delivers consistent acceleration across decoding regimes and serving loads.

### [20] [CLUE: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Unsupervised Event Type Induction and Annotation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12580)
*Pratik Maitra,Lauren Kwon,Qi Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Event ontology is the foundational framework for defining events in a dataset. Event type induction generally involves domain experts who define guidelines for creating event types and their names based on the dataset's domain and scope. However, this process is resource-intensive in terms of annotation costs and is prone to human biases. To alleviate the need for manual event ontology creation, we propose the CLUE framework for event type induction, naming, and annotation. Our main contributions in this work are: 1) designing a novel joint embedding representation for expressing both the verb-centric view and the semantic view of events; 2) event type induction using contrastive loss guided clustering; 3) event naming and refinement. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at this https URL .

### [21] [One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12582)
*Faisal Ladhak,Shantanu Acharya,Santiago Akle Serano,Simeng Sun,Boris Ginsburg,Krishna C Puvvada*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A latent recurrent language model applies a shared block of layers repeatedly, so one checkpoint can trade inference compute for accuracy by changing the loop count. At one loop, however, such models typically fall well short of a non-recurrent model of the same size, a one-loop tax that makes a separate non-recurrent model the better choice whenever latency matters. We present Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR), a recipe for training looped language models without this tax. At one loop, an ELR model costs the same to serve as a non-recurrent model of the same size and, trained on the same data, reaches similar accuracy. Each additional loop then buys more accuracy for more inference compute. Three choices make this work: a gated state update with a learned step size, loop counts mixed within each optimizer update, and conditioning each pass on its loop index and budget. The first two preserve one-loop accuracy, and the third lowers loss at every additional loop. Mixed depths can be introduced late in pretraining to limit the added training cost, and with zero-initialized conditioning added at the switch, this late schedule reaches lower loss than mixed-depth training from scratch. In MoE models, reusing first-loop expert routes on later loops cuts mixed-depth update time by 11.7% with no measurable change in accuracy. At inference, keeping only the last loop's attention KV cache holds attention KV memory at its one-loop level while retaining most of the gain from additional loops. On 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE hybrid models, ELR at one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 points above its matched baseline on a ten-task average, and four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points. Carried through post-training, the recipe yields Koi-4B, a single checkpoint that scores an estimated 18 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at one loop, matching Qwen3.5-4B, and 29 at four loops.

### [22] [Reflective Prompt Optimization of a Deep-Research Agent: A Topic-Disjoint, Multi-Seed Protocol for Measuring Transferable Gains and Prompt-Level Overfitting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12601)
*Elias Lumer,Sahil Sen,Vamse Kumar Subbiah,Kevin Paul*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Prompt optimization is an attractive alternative to reinforcement learning for adapting language-model agents, since it is cheap and produces human-readable artifacts. On factual tasks, however, it carries a failure mode that scalar-reward reinforcement learning does not. An optimizer that reads the training examples can write their answers into the prompt, so an in-distribution gain may be memorization rather than transferable behaviour. We apply reflective prompt evolution (GEPA) to the two system prompts of a multi-agent deep-research agent and evaluate it under a topic-disjoint split in which no topic is shared across train, validation, and test. Held-out citation reward rises by 0.079, from 0.702 to 0.781, with a bootstrap 95\% confidence interval of [0.051, 0.107], and the gain replicates across three seeds (mean 0.107). Nearly half of the winning prompt is a memorized answer key, yet a controlled ablation shows this content earns no reward even on the exact training questions it encodes. The large validation-minus-held-out gap is therefore small-sample selection under a noisy judge, not memorization. Varying the verifier isolates what makes the gain transfer. Decomposed per-dimension feedback is the causal ingredient, and collapsing it to a single scalar reward makes held-out transfer negative. The gain persists under an out-of-family judge and is largely reproduced by a hand-written version of the discovered recipe. Credible evaluation of prompt optimizers therefore requires held-out topics, multiple seeds, and verifier ablations. We release the candidate prompts, lineage diffs, figures, tables, and analysis.

### [23] [GeopoliticalQA: Benchmarking Retrieval and Generation over Intelligence Reports](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12617)
*Veronika Solopova,Ivan Havlytskyi,Viktoria Skorik,Ostap Vykhopen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. We introduce a benchmark for grounded question answering over 415 open-source geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports, comprising 5,525 document-grounded question-answer pairs spanning factual, inferential, comparative, and risk-oriented questions. We propose a document-aware generation pipeline that profiles reports before generating questions and validate dataset quality through expert annotation and an LLM-as-judge protocol. Using the benchmark, we evaluate 15 retrieval systems and six open-weight LLMs for RAG. We find that models perform similarly on document-level retrieval, while at the harder chunk level retrieval quality is not driven by embedding-model scale: bge-m3, a mid-size open encoder matches an order of magnitude larger ones and outperforms commercial embedding APIs. In contrast, answer generation remains challenging even given the gold evidence, particularly for inferential and risk-oriented questions.

### [24] [perturber: A Stateless Service for Semantics-Preserving Text Perturbations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12667)
*Khoi-Nguyen Tran*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language model (LLM) evaluations on clean benchmarks overstate model robustness: real inputs arrive perturbed, and these meaning-preserving variants routinely move model answers. Studying this systematically requires applying perturbations one at a time, reproducibly, and identically wherever they run, yet existing tools couple them to a benchmarking stack rather than packaging them as a reusable transform layer. We present perturber, a stateless service and Python library that applies exactly one semantics-preserving perturbation per call, drawn from a first-party catalog of 68 perturbations across 11 families. It turns on a single primitive, with composition left to the caller chaining calls, so the service and the library produce identical output by construction. We evaluate the tool itself, its correctness, reproducibility, and cost, rather than any model's robustness, measuring meaning-preservation per perturbation rather than assuming it. The demonstration adds a live playground, an introspectable catalog for benchmark selection, and a one-command reproducible evaluation.

### [25] [Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12701)
*Sheza Munir,Ramaravind Kommiya Mothilal,Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Perspectivist NLP has established that annotator positionality shapes labels for subjective tasks, but the field still lacks methods for operationalising it. Positionality is typically operationalised as a demographic form completed at recruitment: a static attribute recorded once and treated as a covariate, on the assumption that the knowledge it indexes is active when the annotator reads an item. This paper treats that assumption as a design problem and asks whether lived experience can instead be primed by the task itself. We introduce AXLE, a pre-annotation stage in which a scenario vignette anchors a short, axis-guided conversation that is synthesised into a first-person micro-narrative and returned to the annotator before labelling begins. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (104 annotators, 30 items, 1,040 annotations) on ambiguous hate speech spanning immigration, religion and gender, elicitation was associated with higher identity resonance and higher sensitivity to harm. It also increased label entropy and lowered inter-annotator agreement: the stage appears to surface plurality rather than manufacture consensus, which distinguishes it from annotator training, whose success criterion is convergence.

### [26] [U4RASD at KnowledgeGraphEval-2026: Ontology-Constrained Encoder and LLM Systems for Arabic Relation Extraction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12742)
*Ahmad Abbas,Hussein Mazeh,Chadi Abou Chakra,Aya Jouni,Mohammad Ballout,Fadi A. Zaraket*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: This paper details our submission to KnowledgeGraphEval 2026 Subtask 2 on directed Arabic relation extraction. We explored encoder-based and large language model approaches for predicting one of 40 relations or no_relation from an Arabic sentence and a subject-object pair. Our encoder systems use typed entity markers and separate relation-existence and relation-classification heads, while our LLM systems fine-tune Yehia and Qwen3.5 with QLoRA and ontology-constrained prediction. Our best system, an ensemble of Yehia-RE, Qwen-RE, and TypedPair, achieved a micro-F1 score of 94.06 and ranked 1st in Subtask 2. Yehia-RE (full-vocabulary) achieved 92.98, while the best encoder and Qwen-RE achieved 92.69 and 91.94 respectively. Our results highlight the importance of constrained prediction and complementary modeling approaches for Arabic relation extraction.

### [27] [MADS: Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation for Robust Conversational Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12757)
*Arkajyoti Chakraborty,Adam Zernik,Ishika Kulkarni,Mudit Arora,Hugo Lin,Justin Chiu,Alessandro Di Bari,Neha Gupta,Andreas Stolcke*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Task-oriented conversational agents remain fragile under realistic conditions, especially when users exhibit non-cooperative behavior. Existing function-calling benchmarks underrepresent adversarial conversation trajectories, thereby limiting the training resources available for developing robust agents. We present MADS (Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation), a synthetic data generation pipeline that produces structured, diverse dialogue trajectories. We inject adversarial conversation, producing validated conversation trajectories that capture realistic, unhappy paths. Using MADS, we construct MADS-Bench: a benchmark spanning six domains, 55 personas, and 1095 conversations, with approximately 66% of conversations containing failure-prone conversation scenarios. We evaluate the robustness of the trained models using a two-stage training approach that combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR).

### [28] [DistressBench: Evaluating Multi-Dimensional Crisis Support in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12758)
*Drew Rein,Patrick Oathout,Vishal Kumar,Udari Madhushani Sehwag*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Language models have been adopted faster than evaluation practices that reliably assess their risks, and a growing share of use is affective rather than informational. Within that traffic users disclose suicide and self-harm (SSH) crises. Existing safety benchmarks score models primarily on refusal, but refusal is not the desired behavior here; the conversation requires a substantive supportive response. We introduce DistressBench, 718 English conversations with clinician-authored user turns spanning 23 SSH subcategories, each paired with a task-specific rubric of weighted atomic criteria across seven dimensions of crisis support and a clinician reference response. A model's score is the weighted average over the criteria its reply satisfies, reading directly as the fraction of required care delivered. The best of 25 frontier models satisfies 88.4% of weighted criteria and the median model 71.4%, against 98.7% for clinician references scored on the same criteria. Pooled across all 25 models, in 35.3% of conversations where a model satisfied every criterion for recognizing the crisis, it failed to route the user toward human help. The shortfall concentrates in the dimensions requiring the model to act rather than withhold. Contrasting each dimension's median model against its best separates capability limits from choices: de-escalation reaches 74.6% in the strongest model against a median of 46.0%, and safety disclaimers 84.6% against 8.3%. Multi-turn conversations score below single-turn ones (68.5% against 74.2%). We release the corpus, rubrics, judge calibration labels, and a companion annex of 20 long-horizon red-team transcripts. These results argue for evaluating crisis safety on the care a model delivers rather than on what it declines to say, and for treating de-escalation and resource routing as deployment requirements.

### [29] [People Making Conversation: Evaluating How Naturally Speech Models Converse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12802)
*Arya Bastani,Iman Modarressi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A conversational speech model has to decide, at every pause, whether to speak. Existing evaluations test boundary detection, policy adherence, or aggregate statistics, not this decision. We place real-time speech systems at 427 pauses and 482 turn ends from 176 unscripted conversations in Seamless Interaction, give each the conversation so far, and score what it generates against what the person did: whether and how soon it speaks at a pause; its latency, length, and wording at a turn end; and whether it can answer a question about the preceding 30 to 120 seconds. Across six systems, the hosted APIs (GPT Realtime, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Grok Voice) respond at almost every pause whichever endpointer they use; only their latency, about 1 to 4 s with silence-based endpointers and about 8 s with semantic turn detection, decides whether the words land inside the pause. The full-duplex models (PersonaPlex, Moshi) are the only systems that regularly stay silent and the only ones that interrupt within a human reaction time. Hosted systems reply longer than the person. Given the history as text, hosted systems recall 41 to 60% of conversation facts under a Claude Opus 5.5 judge and 19 to 26% under a strict word matcher; hearing it as audio, full-duplex models recall 17 to 22% and 12 to 15%. We release the labels, points, harness, and every output.

### [30] [When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12823)
*Yisheng Li,Dongming Han,Hongkun Pan,Bingcheng Mao,Zijian Wang,Yunlong Mao,Wei Tong,Sheng Zhong*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Web agents increasingly browse, interpret, and act on web content on behalf of users. In many realistic workflows, however, the visual evidence they consume is not neutral: charts and dashboards can be misleading, shaping judgments without issuing any explicit malicious instruction. Unlike chart question answering, Web Agents treat charts as intermediate evidence whose misinterpretation can propagate into concrete downstream actions --- a reliability risk that remains underexplored. We introduce MisVisAgentBench, the first paired executable benchmark for evaluating how misleading visualizations affect Web Agent execution. It comprises 280 task instances in matched clean--misleading pairs that differ only in chart evidence. We further provide a diagnostic framework that isolates misleading-induced failures from baseline task difficulty (Zhu et al., 2025) and captures execution-level effects such as extra browsing steps and decision hesitation. Across thirteen vision-language Web Agents, replacing clean charts with misleading counterparts reduces the average task success rate by more than 34 percentage points. Moreover, these failures predominantly follow the targeted misleading action branch, suggesting that deceptive charts systematically redirect rather than randomly disrupt agent decisions. These results reveal that visualization robustness is a critical yet understudied dimension of Web Agent safety and reliability.

### [31] [Fear Is Not Always Fear: Variation in Emotion Label Equivalence Across Datasets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12841)
*Emily Öhman,Anna Koufakou*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Emotion classifiers are routinely applied beyond their training data, on the assumption that same-named labels such as fear or surprise mean the same thing across resources. We test this assumption for five labels shared by GoEmotions, XED, and BRIGHTER, comparing models on identical inputs and under cross-corpus transfer. On the same texts, one fear classifier flags 71% as fearful and another 8%, yet the two largely agree on how the texts rank. Across 30 resource-label comparisons, training-label prevalence explains about half of this kind of scale mismatch, and a fitted intercept removes most of it. What recalibration cannot repair is larger: transferred models lose 55% of native discrimination in aggregate, agreement in ranking between classifiers is only weakly related to that loss, and for surprise the resources disagree about which texts express the emotion. The choice of training resource can therefore change conclusions: on two external tweet collections, BRIGHTER- and XED-trained classifiers give opposite answers about which shows more surprise, even after rank normalization, with intervals excluding zero in both directions. A shared emotion label name does not establish an interchangeable measurement target.

### [32] [Unreliable Narrator Framing as a Cost-effective Mechanism for Satire Explanation of Australian and American Satirical News](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12863)
*Kanay Gupta,David Y. Liu,Aditya Joshi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Satirical news is a unique form of misinformation: it is intended to be humorous by the original publication source but can be misinterpreted. Explanation of satirical news articles is challenging because recent and local context needs to be incorporated. This is a pilot study that explores explanation generation for satirical news articles from Australia and compares them alongside those from USA. The paper demonstrates that framing explanations on unreliable narrator theory on open-weights models can be a feasible, cost-effective alternative to frontier models. We find that models identify the satirical tropes more accurately on the American source than the Australian one. This work results in a novel dataset and an evaluation benchmark for satirical explanation.

### [33] [Time Delay System for Sequence Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12864)
*Youshan Zhang,Jialu Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Existing sequence models share a critical limitation: they lack an explicit, interpretable mechanism for content-aware temporal recall. LSTMs compress everything into a single hidden state, thereby losing information about specific past events. Transformers attend to all tokens indiscriminately at quadratic cost, while state-space models like Mamba compress history into a fixed-dimensional state without explicit content-addressable memory. To address this gap, we introduce a novel framework grounded in nonlinear time-delay systems, in which the effective delay is dynamically estimated based on the semantic similarity between current and historical inputs. Our approach features three key innovations: (i) a differentiable semantic lag estimator that computes content-aware soft attention weights over history, producing a weighted historical context and similarity score; (ii) a diagonal state space with closed-form cumulative sum solution, achieving O(1) per-step complexity with no sequential loops; and (iii) an interpretable fuzzy semantic modulation mechanism that learns context-dependent rules for balancing instantaneous processing versus historical recall, where rule centers correspond to prototypical semantic contexts. Experimental results on text classification and generation outperform state-of-the-art methods.

### [34] [Temporal Evidence Forests for Long-Horizon Multi-Party Conversational Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12874)
*Junyou Guo,Chongyang Tao,Yan He,Yong Wang,Shuai Ma*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Long-term memory has been widely adopted in LLM-based agents to support persistent interaction and personalized assistance. Long-term multi-party interactions, however, accumulate substantially more detailed information, with decisions repeatedly updated and states evolving across participants and interaction stages. Temporal structure is therefore crucial for tracing such memories: relevant information often appears densely within short intervals, while transitions among different states are anchored by a strict temporal order. Existing temporally aware memory frameworks primarily store time as metadata or use temporal signals to guide retrieval over preconstructed memory structures, without using temporal structure to both recover locally concentrated evidence and reconstruct its complete event progression. To address these limitations, we propose T-Mem, a temporal-structure-based memory framework that preserves interactions and organizes query-relevant evidence through two temporal mechanisms. Temporal Evidence Discovery exploits the local concentration of related messages to recover overlooked evidence, while Temporal Memory Structuring models state transitions and supporting relations over time and compresses low-information spans within the resulting forest. Evidence Forest Linearization then serializes the structured evidence for answer generation. Experiments on two long-term multi-party memory benchmarks demonstrate that T-Mem consistently outperforms competitive memory frameworks across LLMs, parameter settings, domains, and query types.

### [35] [SEEDS: Preview-Guided Evidence Admission for Search Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12932)
*Jiajin Liu,Chenxi Xu,Dongzhe Fan,Yuanfu Sun,Qiaoyu Tan*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Search agents extend large reasoning models with multi-round access to external knowledge, yet most existing systems largely conflate retrieving evidence with consuming it. Retrieved documents are commonly incorporated according to fixed or rank-based policies, despite the fact that evidence utility is conditioned on the agent's current reasoning state. Consequently, a lower-ranked candidate may be critical for the current step, while a higher-ranked candidate may provide redundant, irrelevant, or misleading information. We formulate this overlooked problem as evidence admission, which asks, at each search step, which retrieved candidates should be allowed to enter the agent's evolving reasoning context. To enable such selective control, we introduce SEEDS (Selective Evidence Entry During Search), a preview-guided evidence admission framework for search agents. SEEDS first exposes lightweight previews of retrieved candidates and then lets the agent jointly determine which candidates and how many should be fully inspected, conditioned on its current reasoning state. Unlike fixed or adaptive prefix policies, SEEDS can select arbitrary subsets with flexible cardinality, and it can be instantiated directly with an existing reasoning agent or further optimized through learning. Across nine knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks under both local corpus and live web search, SEEDS consistently improves search effectiveness while substantially reducing full-evidence consumption. Experimental analyses show that SEEDS more effectively selects useful candidates beyond the corresponding retrieval prefix. These results establish evidence admission as a complementary dimension of agentic search, separating what information is retrieved from what information is ultimately allowed to shape reasoning.

### [36] [Language Models Have Interpretable Narrative Mechanisms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12989)
*David Yiyang Liu,Aditya Joshi,Paul Dawson,Andrew Piper*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: We investigate whether language models contain internal components that contribute to representing narrativity, the degree to which a text exhibits narrative properties. Across GPT-2-Small, Gemma-2-2B, and Llama-3.1-8B, we identify attention heads, MLP neurons, and sparse autoencoder features whose activations correlate with narrativity. Ablating selected neuron and feature sets increases next-token prediction loss more for high-narrativity than for low-narrativity texts, and reduces the narrativity of open-ended generations. On downstream benchmarks, the largest effects occur in story completion and narrative question answering, although they vary across models and languages; results on confabulation and hallucination benchmarks are mixed. These findings provide causal evidence that selected sets of narrative-associated components contribute to model behaviour, while their internal organisation, relation to narrative theory, and broader functions remain open questions.

### [37] [Evaluating LLM Creativity through Long-Tail Performance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12998)
*Yichen Wang,Tenghao Huang,Vishakh Padmakumar,Mina Lee*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Creativity benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) vary widely in task and metric design. This raises the question of whether they capture a common notion of creativity. We propose that this shared target can be formalized as task-specific performance in the long tail of a reference input-output distribution, which describes how common input-output pairs are relative to a chosen source of text. We ground this proposition in the novelty-quality product formulation and evaluate it empirically across 15 benchmarks and 26 open-weight models, using n-gram absence from the pretraining data as a novelty proxy. Our results show that creativity benchmarks lie further in the tail regions than standard benchmarks. Moreover, on both creativity and standard benchmarks, model rankings from higher-tail subsets of each benchmark align more closely with human creativity judgments in LM-Arena. Building on these findings, we introduce q@Tail($\alpha$), a lower-cost creativity diagnostic that measures mean task quality on the tail fraction of an existing benchmark. Applying it to creativity-promoting methods reveals substantial room to improve LLM creativity through stronger tail performance.

### [38] [Evo$^2$: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13025)
*Chejian Xu,Shujian Zhang,Wenxuan Zhou,John Lambert,Beck Chen,Bo Li,Andrew Hard,Rajiv Mathews*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Self-evolving agents are increasingly used to improve language model systems without human intervention through either weight updates or harness improvements. Existing approaches typically pursue these directions separately: some methods update model weights using self-generated experience, while others rewrite the harness that defines how an agent uses prompts, tools, context, and execution feedback. However, these approaches overlook the relationship between model weights and the agent harness. To connect these processes and ensure effective and smooth agent self-evolving, we propose Evo$^2$, a framework for weight-harness co-evolution. For harness updates, we design a unified dual-role pipeline that a single policy serves as both a Proposer, which writes harness edits, and a Reflector, which diagnoses their effects and guides revision. For weight updates, harness modifications and their execution outcomes guide the training of both the Proposer and the Reflector. We further develop EvoTIDE, a training pipeline that recovers usable trajectories through edit extraction and prefix continuation, then combines SFT with interleaved GRPO across the two roles. Extensive experiments across three coding benchmarks demonstrate that Evo$^2$ significantly outperforms existing self-evolution methods. It achieves 82.1% on Polyglot and 48.3% on SWE-bench Verified, compared with 62.6% and 41.0% for the strongest baseline, respectively. We also show that the evolved harnesses transfer to different tasks without further evolution and rank first in cross-benchmark evaluations. Our dual-role harness improvement framework is also able to extend to self-evolution with proprietary models, improving a GPT-5-mini agent's performance from 24.4% to 48.3%. These results demonstrate the applicability of the framework Evo$^2$ across domains and its broad transferability across models and tasks.

### [39] [RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13041)
*Ke Wan,Chen Chen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Recurrent-depth language models improve inference-time reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared network to refine internal representations, but the additional recurrent computation also increases inference cost. This overhead is particularly pronounced during long-context prefill, where the full input sequence is repeatedly processed across recurrent depth. Weight-and-activation quantization offers a natural way to accelerate this computation through lower-precision arithmetic, yet repeatedly applying quantized computation introduces numerical perturbations that accumulate along the recurrent trajectory. We systematically analyze how such errors propagate across recurrent depth and show that quantization errors introduced earlier are attenuated by more subsequent recurrent steps and therefore have a smaller effect on the final representation. Matched-budget experiments strongly support this prediction, showing that placing quantized computation earlier in recurrent depth consistently yields the best fidelity. Based on this insight, we introduce RAMP (Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision), which performs early recurrent refinement using low-precision weight-and-activation computation and restores high precision for terminal refinement. Across context lengths up to 4K, RAMP preserves near-full-precision prefill quality while achieving up to 1.16x end-to-end first-prefill speedup on an NVIDIA H100, corresponding to a 13.9% latency reduction.

### [40] [CliQ-RRG: Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13059)
*Chandravardhan Singh Raghaw,Shahid Shafi Dar,Arnav Nishith Sharma,Shrey Modi,Nagendra Kumar*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Radiology reports are essential for diagnostic reasoning and patient care, yet their manual preparation is time-consuming and cognitively demanding. Automatic radiology report generation (RRG) offers a scalable alternative, but existing models often produce lengthy, unstructured narratives that overlook diagnostic cues and multi-view information. We present Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation (CliQ-RRG), a unified two-stage framework for interpretable and clinically grounded reporting. In Stage 1, CliQ-RRG employs a Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment module that aligns image and text representations using predicted disease embeddings, reinforced by a Prior-Guided Attention Module (PrAM) to capture multi-view dependencies across current and prior scans. In Stage 2, GraphRAG-guided retrieval augments intermediate textual representations with graph-grounded clinical evidence, and a large language model restructures them into concise, interpretable question-answer (QA) pairs with diagnostic summaries. Experiments on two public chest X-ray benchmarks demonstrate that CliQ-RRG consistently outperforms prior methods across both lexical and clinical metrics, generating accurate and clinically coherent QA-style radiology reports. Code is available at: this https URL .

In Stage 2, GraphRAG-guided retrieval augments intermediate textual representations with graph-grounded clinical evidence, and a large language model restructures them into concise, interpretable question-answer (QA) pairs with diagnostic summaries. Experiments on two public chest X-ray benchmarks demonstrate that CliQ-RRG consistently outperforms prior methods across both lexical and clinical metrics, generating accurate and clinically coherent QA-style radiology reports. ### [41] [KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13060)
*Taiga Ikeda,Daisuke Miyashita,Jun Deguchi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: KV-cache reuse in large language model serving is commonly limited to exact prompt prefixes, preventing reuse when the same retrieved document appears after different system prompts, conversation histories, or dynamic metadata. We present KV-Repurpose, an open-source, vLLM-based system for developing and evaluating segment-wise KV-cache reuse beyond exact prefixes. The system combines cache-aware segment scheduling, prompt construction, capacity management, workload generation, and runtime monitoring. Experiments on long-context benchmarks show that naive segment reuse largely preserves output quality for single-document question answering and summarization, while exposing clear limitations in cross-document reasoning. Under a Zipfian RAG-style workload in which 20% of requests share a fixed prefix, KV-Repurpose achieves a substantially higher token-level cache hit rate than prefix caching at the same 30 GB cache capacity, 63.9% versus 3.3%, resulting in lower TTFT. Even with 1 TB of cache capacity, prefix caching reaches only a 17.9% hit rate in this workload. Source code is available under the Apache-2.0 license at this https URL .

### [42] [From 2.1M Hours of Raw Broadcast Audio to Finnish Speech SSL: Confidence Filtering and Architectural Analysis at Scale](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13102)
*Yaroslav Getman,Tamás Grósz,Tommi Lehtonen,Mikko Kurimo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Broadcast archives offer scale and diversity for self-supervised learning (SSL) but contain substantial noisy, non-speech, and multilingual content. Prior work typically relies on voice activity detection or language identification (LID) to extract speech, ensuring presence rather than quality. Whether and how to filter unlabeled speech by quality for SSL, particularly from noisy broadcasts, remains underexplored. We present a large-scale Finnish SSL study starting from 2.1M hours of unconstrained broadcast audio. We propose automatic speech recognition (ASR) confidence as a proxy for pretraining data quality and show 3-7% relative WER improvements over LID-based filtering despite a smaller training set. We further address the lack of controlled architectural comparisons in speech SSL by evaluating Transformer, Macaron-Net, Conformer, and E-Branchformer at matched parameter budgets. Our models improve upon prior Finnish SSL baselines, particularly at Base scale and out-of-domain.

### [43] [BenCoDiC: A Large-Scale Contextual Cyberbullying Corpus for Bengali Political News Discourse FULL VERSION](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13121)
*Md. Nesarul Hoque,Rudra Pratap Deb Nath,Umme Salma,Shima Chakraborty,Md. Hanif Seddiqui*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Cyberbullying is a growing concern in online communities, yet existing Bengali corpora remain limited in contextual information, annotation transparency, scale, accessibility, and support for multidimensional analysis, thereby hindering robust detection and comprehensive study of harasser behaviors and networks. To address these gaps, we introduce the Bengali Contextual and Diverse Cyberbullying (\textit{BenCoDiC}) corpus, a publicly available contextual cyberbullying resource for Bengali political news discourse comprising 50,250 textual instances collected from 100 YouTube videos and their associated discussions. The corpus preserves caption--comment--reply relationships and is organized through a nine-dimensional star schema covering users, videos, textual content, context, time, engagement, political parties, target identities, and language categories. Five AI chatbots were initially evaluated for annotation but did not meet the predefined reliability criterion. Consequently, a two-tier human annotation process with expert verification was adopted, achieving Fleiss' $\kappa=0.86$ and Krippendorff's $\alpha=0.86$. Statistical analyses characterize the corpus, while transformer-based experiments show that incorporating conversational context yields modest but consistent improvements over isolated-text classification. \textit{BenCoDiC} supports context-aware cyberbullying detection and perpetrator-oriented behavioral and network analysis. The corpus is available at this https URL .

### [44] [SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157)
*Shengze Huang,Zihao Tang,Jinluan Yang,Xin Yu,Zhenghao Lin,Xiao Liu,Zengxuan Wen,Yeyun Gong,Haizhen Huang,Weiwei Deng,Feng Sun,Qi Zhang,Fei Wu,Kun Kuang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reinforcement learning (RL) for search agents often suffers from evidence fabrication, a failure mode where agents bypass external information ($E_{ext}$) and fabricate an incorrect answer. We argue that this fabrication arises from an over-reliance on unreliable internal knowledge ($E_{int}$) as shortcuts due to the inherent opacity of reasoning trajectories. To address this, we propose SOAR (SOurce-Aware Reinforcement learning), a paradigm that transforms monolithic reasoning into source-explicit trajectories. SOAR (i) disentangles $E_{ext}$ and $E_{int}$ into parallel, observable streams via a Source-Aware Workflow, and (ii) incorporates Source-Consistent Reward to guide the policy evolution. By making information-source attribution explicit, SOAR enables precise credit assignment between different knowledge streams. Evaluations show that SOAR outperforms baselines on 3B and 7B backbones by 7.3% and 5.4%, while reducing evidence fabrication by 74.8%. These confirm that SOAR significantly improves performance on knowledge-intensive benchmarks while effectively mitigating evidence fabrication, fostering more faithful and grounded reasoning with enhanced robustness.

### [45] [Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13166)
*Shun Zou,Ziyu Ma,Yi Zou,Yong Wang,Lin Chen,Zehui Chen,Guanhua Chen,Xiangxiang Chu,Feng Zhao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Terminal agents are moving beyond local operations toward completing real-world professional tasks. Short trajectories can demonstrate commands and tool calls, but they do not fully show how agents accumulate evidence through exploration, use it to inform judgments, continually adjust strategies based on feedback, and turn intermediate results into final deliverables. High-quality long-horizon trajectories capture these agentic behavioral patterns and their connections within a single problem-solving process, providing richer experience for sustained autonomous work. However, environment synthesis may complete or simplify the key work underlying these patterns in advance and thus remove the need for exploration, implementation, and verification that the agent was meant to perform. To address this, we introduce TerminalHorizon, a fully automated data synthesis engine for long-horizon terminal agents. Starting from real-world professional work, it uses independent execution to identify key work omitted during construction and uses the resulting evidence to guide environment reconstruction. To extend these patterns across stages, it progressively expands tasks under the same goal, introducing new requirements that build on prior results and call for further exploration and improvement. Using this engine, we construct 1.5K task environments and perform supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-27B on the resulting dataset to obtain TerminalHorizon-27B. We achieve substantial performance gains on all 12 benchmarks spanning coding-agent tasks, agentic tasks in real-world production settings, and general reasoning. Multiple RSI case studies, each with a 12-hour research budget, further demonstrate the model's ability to continue experimenting beyond an initial solution, improve its methods based on feedback, and retain effective improvements in its final deliverables.

### [46] [PreSTO: Predictive Subtree Prefetching for Fast LLM Power Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13171)
*Nan Jiang,Panagiotis Theodoropoulos,Wei Deng*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Power sampling improves large language model (LLM) reasoning at test time by sampling from a sharpened version of the base model's distribution. Its sampler, PowerMH, is slow because its Metropolis--Hastings (MH) updates are sequential: each accept/reject decision sets the state from which the next proposal is generated. Prior work reduces this cost by changing the sampler or the model (e.g., sequential Monte Carlo, approximate lookahead, distillation). We propose Predictive SubTree Prefetching (PreSTO), which accelerates PowerMH by prefetching future proposals and provably leaves its MH transition kernel unchanged. PreSTO views future MH outcomes as a tree of accept/reject decisions: in each model call, it generates the proposals of a \textit{prefetched subtree} of this tree in one batch, then follows the realized path with the original MH acceptance rule. We also observe that MH reaches only a sparse, nearly unary part of each prefetched subtree, we further design a \textit{predictive traversal rule} that chooses the subtree to maximize the predicted number of completed transitions. Across seven datasets and five base LLMs, PreSTO achieves median speedups of $1.71\times$, $1.91\times$, and $2.33\times$ on PowerMH and its follow-ups EntropyCut and MultiTryMH, respectively; on the first two, it makes a median of $3.9\times$ fewer model calls, each only $2.1\times$ longer. On LCB V6 with Qwen3.5-9B, the predictive traversal rule is a further $1.25\times$--$1.37\times$ faster than the default breadth-first traversal.
