### [47] [SharP: Soft and Hard Prompt-Guided Augmentation with LLM for Low Resource Fake News Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13207)
*Ziyu Luo,Wei Li,Haoping Huang,Kecheng Liu,Min Gao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Fake news detection under low resource conditions is challenged by the scarcity of labeled data and the difficulty of capturing subtle deceptive patterns. In this work, we focus on low resource fake news detection, where only a small labeled set is available for training, while evaluation is performed under a fixed and unchanged test protocol. This setting is motivated by costly, ambiguous fact-checking and emerging topics and domains that are poorly covered by existing benchmarks. Existing data augmentation methods, such as synonym substitution, generative adversarial networks, and large language model (LLM)-based generation, often produce fluent but overly generic content, lacking the task-specific relevance needed for accurate detection. To address this, we propose SharP, a boundary-aware text generation framework guided by soft and hard prompts, which leverages LLMs as tools adapted to produce task-specific synthetic samples. SharP employs a dual prompt mechanism: hard prompts provide structured guidance and factual constraints, while soft prompts introduce learned semantic patterns from the data. These two types of prompts are combined to guide the generation process, enabling the model to produce samples that closely align with the characteristics of news. To further enhance detection performance, we incorporate a boundary-aware strategy that steers generation toward areas where the classifier is less confident, helping to clarify subtle distinctions between real and fake content. In addition, we adopt a dual objective optimization that balances semantic alignment with the source data and classifier feedback. This encourages the generation of samples that are both domain-consistent and helpful for refining decision boundaries, ultimately improving model robustness and generalization in low resource fake news detection.

### [48] [Host-Aware Web Crawling for LLM Pretraining Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13321)
*Malte Ostendorff*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Web crawling is a major source of large language model (LLM) pretraining data, yet data-selection pipelines discard a large share of crawled pages. We investigate how a crawler should allocate its budget across and within hosts to collect more high-quality pretraining data. Combining document-level quality classifier scores, web-graph centrality metrics, and Common Crawl's per-host crawl coverage, we find that roughly half of the variation in classifier scores occurs between hosts. In the crawls we analyze, a few pages from a host also provide a useful estimate of the quality of its remaining pages. Common Crawl uses harmonic centrality, a graph centrality metric, to guide its crawl allocation. In our simulations, using centrality to choose which hosts to crawl yields limited gains over random ordering and performs worse for some classifiers. For deciding how deeply to crawl each host, sampling a few pages and then fetching more from hosts with higher-scoring samples collects several times more high-quality pages per fetch than uniform depth or centrality-based allocation. Finally, Common Crawl's observed per-host coverage has little correlation with the evaluated quality signals. We estimate that tens of millions of high-quality pages remain among known but uncrawled URLs in each crawl examined, with most concentrated on a small share of hosts.

### [49] [Test-Time Memory Construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13348)
*Zijun Wang,Yifan Ji,Haidong Xin,Zhenghao Liu,Yukun Yan,Zulong Chen,Yu Gu,Ge Yu,Maosong Sun*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large Language Models (LLMs) struggle to answer questions over long interaction histories, where relevant evidence may be scattered across distant sessions. Existing memory systems typically construct and maintain sophisticated memory representations offline, before user queries are observed, incurring substantial overhead and limiting their ability to adapt memory construction to query-specific information needs. In this paper, we propose T$^2$Mem, a Test-Time Memory construction framework that defers memory construction to inference and progressively builds memory along the reasoning process. Specifically, T$^2$Mem extracts lightweight episode-level metadata offline to capture key events and temporal associations as retrieval cues, while retaining links to the original interactions to facilitate the reconstruction of dependencies across episodes. At test time, the LLM adaptively retrieves and organizes metadata and raw interactions, progressively constructing query-specific memory as reasoning unfolds. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval show the effectiveness of T$^2$Mem by consistently outperforming strong baselines across different backbone LLMs while substantially reducing the overhead of memory construction. Further analysis demonstrates that deferring memory construction to inference enables the memory construction process to dynamically adapt to the information needs of individual queries. All code is available at this https URL .

### [50] [From Structure to Validity: Mechanism-Guided Generation and Refinement of LLM Rubrics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13375)
*Feifei Qian,Xuan Chen,Lixin Cui,Chaoyang Mei,Fanlin Meng,Shuyao Xiao,Ming Cui,Junxi Yin,Lu Bai*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Rubrics have been widely used to evaluate and optimize language models on open-ended tasks. However, existing work primarily focuses on generating better rubrics, with limited understanding of what makes rubric design effective. In this work, we conduct a systematic mechanistic analysis of rubric design across criterion organization, criterion operationalization, and score aggregation. Our analysis shows that structural organization enables more comprehensive criterion construction, semantic specification alone does not ensure effective criterion-level judgments, and sophisticated score aggregation provides limited additional gains. Guided by these findings, we introduce Adaptive Rubric Tree Search with Hybrid refinement (ARTS-Hybrid), which combines adaptive tree construction with semantic-first, response-calibrated refinement. Experiments across benchmarks show that ARTS-Hybrid improves both end-to-end evaluation performance and intrinsic rubric quality. Further experiments suggest that, beyond evaluation, rubrics generated by ARTS-Hybrid provide effective signals for model optimization.

### [51] [MoPrO-SD: Modular Prompt Optimization for Stance Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13386)
*Meysam Sabbaghan,Nikesh Gyawali,Arman Zareian Jahromi,Sebastian Loera-Lozano,Doina Caragea,Cornelia Caragea*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Stance detection remains challenging for large language models (LLMs) due to implicit opinions, sarcasm, and context-dependent expressions of stance. Although automatic prompt optimization offers an alternative to fine-tuning without updating model parameters, existing structured approaches are not specifically designed around stance-label semantics and class-specific ambiguities. We introduce MoPrO-SD, a stance-specific prompt optimization framework that decomposes prompts into functional semantic modules and refines them sequentially using LLM-based feedback. We study three refinement strategies: instruction-only optimization (I), instruction with reasoning (I+R), and instruction with per-example reasoning (I+R+E), using class-conditioned errors for stance-label refinement. We also introduce VaccineStance, a new human-annotated benchmark for vaccine stance detection. Experiments across four datasets and five open-weight LLMs show that MoPrO-SD improves upon the human-written Base prompt in many settings. On SemEval-2016, class-conditioned feedback achieves higher mean Macro-F1 than pooled feedback for four of five backbones. Both reasoning-based strategies, I+R and I+R+E, achieve strong performance, with their relative effectiveness varying across models and datasets, while remaining competitive with recent prompt optimization methods. The MoPrO-SD code and VaccineStance dataset are available on GitHub.

Although automatic prompt optimization offers an alternative to fine-tuning without updating model parameters, existing structured approaches are not specifically designed around stance-label semantics and class-specific ambiguities. We introduce MoPrO-SD, a stance-specific prompt optimization framework that decomposes prompts into functional semantic modules and refines them sequentially using LLM-based feedback. We study three refinement strategies: instruction-only optimization (I), instruction with reasoning (I+R), and instruction with per-example reasoning (I+R+E), using class-conditioned errors for stance-label refinement. We also introduce VaccineStance, a new human-annotated benchmark for vaccine stance detection. Experiments across four datasets and five open-weight LLMs show that MoPrO-SD improves upon the human-written Base prompt in many settings. On SemEval-2016, class-conditioned feedback achieves higher mean Macro-F1 than pooled feedback for four of five backbones. Both reasoning-based strategies, I+R and I+R+E, achieve strong performance, with their relative effectiveness varying across models and datasets, while remaining competitive with recent prompt optimization methods. The MoPrO-SD code and VaccineStance dataset are available on GitHub.

### [52] [Towards the Roof of the World: NLP Progress in Tibetan Languages](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13398)
*Xi Cao,Yijie Li,Yuan Sun,Shiwei Dong,Zeguang Huang,Nuo Qun*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Tibetan, spoken by some seven million people on and around the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, remains underrepresented in natural language processing (NLP). We present, to our knowledge, the first peer-reviewed systematic bibliometric survey of Tibetan NLP: 140 publications from 2004 to 2026 in the ACL Anthology and DBLP, annotated for venue type, research area, first-affiliation country, and resource release. Output has grown rapidly, with 84% of the publications appearing since 2018, and has expanded bottom-up along the NLP pipeline, from corpora and word segmentation through script, speech, and applications to large language models (LLMs). Researchers based in China first-authored 87% of the publications, which span all 25 represented research areas, whereas work from other countries concentrates on Classical Tibetan. We argue that this full-pipeline paradigm, realized under the compounded constraints of a complex script, dialectal diversity, and geographic remoteness, offers a reference model for other low-resource languages of the Global South. We also identify gaps in dialect coverage, responsible NLP, native and comparable evaluation, cross-community visibility, and resource release (only 29% of the publications release data, code, or models), and recommend open science, shared standards, and community participation for the LLM era.

### [53] [Towards Enriching Design-Time Models with Evidence from Simulation and Operational Activities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13456)
*Barbara da Silva Oliveira,Julien Deantoni,Nicolas Ferry*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Cyber-Physical Systems are developed through multiple model based activities, comprising several stages of development. As the development progresses through simulation, experimentation, and operation, observations of system execution may reveal missing, uncertain, or invalid design knowledge. The path from execution results to persistent design-time enrichment, however, is often implicit. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing an evidence driven workflow for systematically transferring knowledge produced during simulation and operation back into design-time models. We demonstrate the workflow using an Influence Model, a design-time artefact used to represent how design artefacts and environmental factors jointly affect system response properties, using a sign-following robot use case. We show how simulation evidence can enrich Influence Models by supporting participant pruning decisions, interaction characterisation, influence-function abstraction, and validity-scope information. The application demonstrates the feasibility of the workflow for simulation-based evidence and its potential benefits to improve design-time reasoning and feedback in subsequent development iterations.

### [54] [A Better Metric Will Not Save You: What You Compare Beats How You Compare It](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13476)
*Noureddine Khaous,Guillaume Wisniewski*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Representational similarity measures (RSA, CKA, Procrustes) are chosen for the transformations they treat as irrelevant, and all of them take the set of conditions as given. That set is fixed by two decisions, which inputs are admitted and how they are grouped, both taken before the matrix a measure operates on exists: no invariance property reaches them. We measure what they are worth where the arrangement the conditions ought to have is known independently of the systems compared, the acoustic organisation of vowels, across fifteen languages and twenty-seven representations. Changing which categories are compared, at a fixed number of them, moves the gap between two representations by more than twice the effect being measured, while changing how many moves it not at all. In this setting rankings of models are identified under these choices, and rankings across languages are not.

### [55] [Proactive Agentic Orchestration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13485)
*Xueyang Feng,Chaozhuo Li,Xiaohe Bo,Jiakai Tang,Chenxi Li,Qiwei Ye,Xu Chen*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Agentic orchestration delegates tasks to sub-agents with independent contexts, providing a key path to extending the effective execution horizon of large language model agents. However, existing orchestration methods face two limitations: in execution, current methods fix sub-agents' goals and harnesses at creation time, limiting their adaptability to dynamic real-world environments; in optimization, sparse and delayed feedback constrains effective learning of the orchestration policy. To address these limitations, we introduce POrchestra, an on-the-fly proactive agentic orchestration framework. It allows sub-agents to proactively communicate with the orchestrator at any logical point to request harness adjustments while maintaining continuity of local execution. This mechanism not only enables sub-agents to adapt seamlessly to dynamic environments but also naturally inspires On-Policy Orchestration Distillation (OPOD) based on hindsight feedback. OPOD attributes sub-agents' proactive revision requests back to preceding orchestration decisions to derive targeted improvement signals, and leverages these signals as process supervision alongside the final reward to optimize the orchestration policy. We evaluate POrchestra on three long-horizon agent benchmarks spanning deep research, dynamic digital assistance, and software engineering. POrchestra improves task success by an average of 9.1% relative to the strongest baseline; combined with OPOD, it improves small-orchestrator success by an average of 10.0% relative to existing training baselines. POrchestra also achieves a more favorable cost-performance trade-off. Our code is publicly available at this https URL .

### [56] [Personalization Without Stereotyping: Do Speech LLMs Know When to Turn a Deaf Ear?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13550)
*Kshitij Ambilduke,Caroline Brun,Thibaut Thonet,Vassilina Nikoulina,Marcely Zanon Boito*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Recent speech LLMs can leverage rich paralinguistic cues, enabling more complex and personalized interactions. However, little work investigates how this sensitivity can lead to stereotyping, and existing evaluations largely measure demographic disparities without distinguishing beneficial personalization from stereotypical behavior. We introduce BASIS-Bench, a benchmark designed to disentangle these two aspects through three axes: (1) demographic robustness, measuring disparities in content-based tasks across speakers and demographic classification capabilities; (2) stereotypical bias, measuring whether perceived demographic cues trigger unprompted stereotypical behavior; and (3) personalization, measuring whether models can tailor responses to demographic characteristics when explicitly requested. We evaluate eight recent speech LLMs and find that, despite often recognizing demographic cues, most fail to translate them into appropriate personalization. Explicit demographic labels improve personalization but also amplify stereotypical associations already present in the textual backbones. These findings highlight the need to train speech LLMs not only to perceive demographic cues, but to learn when they should shape their responses.

### [57] [Measuring Artifact Reliance in Machine-Generated Text Detectors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13583)
*Anastasia Voznyuk,Andrey Grabovoy*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Detectors of machine-generated text score almost perfectly on scientific-literature benchmarks, implying we can reliably distinguish with these detectors human and machine-generated documents. We looked at ten scientific-document subsets from six popular resources, and on several of them that apparent ease is a side effect of how the documents were put together. A logistic regression using 27 superficial features reached 0.833-0.997 macro-F1, and on the three arXiv subsets it outperformed every detector we evaluate with F1-scores 0.951-0.997. The strongest cue to the detector is the PDF extraction artifact: human texts retain their original line breaks, whereas generated texts are extracted as a single block of prose. This cue, together with three other formatting features, tell the classes apart at 0.996 AUC. To distinguish benchmarks that contain such a signal from detectors that rely on one, we introduce format counterfactuals: just re-wrapping a machine-written abstract without changing a single word reverses 20-27% of a public detector's correct decisions. Normalizing formatting before training reduces the generalization gap from 0.32 to 0.22. On format-clean benchmarks, it also raises out-of-domain macro-F1 from 0.33 to 0.65 for detectors trained on artifact-containing subsets.

### [58] [zip2zip++: Towards Inference-Time Token Compression with Minimal Quality Loss](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13605)
*Saibo Geng,Andrea Gentilini,Xinxian Ma,Nathan Ranchin,Yunzhen Yao,Robert West*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Dynamic vocabularies built on-the-fly via Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) compression let a language model represent the same text in fewer tokens, but prior work shows that this efficiency comes at a cost to reasoning and perplexity. We show that this quality gap is not a fundamental price of compression but can be substantially closed through targeted improvements to the compression layer and LZW codec, without modifying the underlying pretrained language model. Our analysis reveals four key issues: (1) LZW's compression algorithm creates an implicit conflict between the input embedding and the output embedding, a tension that a single shared embedding cannot resolve; (2) naively applying RoPE to LZW-compressed sequences ignores that merged tokens can span multiple tokens; (3) merging certain tokens (notably digits) disproportionately hurts downstream accuracy; and (4) dynamic vocabularies introduce an inherent segmentation ambiguity that confounds standard evaluation. We address these through decoupled input/output dynamic embedding layer, size-aware RoPE positioning, and a modified LZW codec supporting selective merges and multi-view segmentations. Across four models, our recipe improves perplexity on every corpus we evaluated as well as mathematical reasoning accuracy, closing roughly half the quality gap between zip2zip and the uncompressed baseline at a similar compression ratio on general text. This represents a significant step toward lossless adaptive-vocabulary compression for language models.

### [59] [BLiMPPI: Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Polarity Items](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13607)
*Arzu Burcu Güven,Anna Rogers,Leonie Weissweiler,Joakim Nivre,Rob van der Goot*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Negative polarity items (NPIs), such as "anymore" and "ever", are grammatical only in select environments, predominantly in the context of negation. Because their grammaticality depends on both syntax and semantics, they have a rich, multilingual literature in theoretical linguistics, yet work on NPIs in language models is almost entirely confined to English. We introduce BLiMPPI, a multilingual evaluation suite of over 12,000 NPI minimal pairs in 33 languages, built by a pipeline that discovers NPIs in Universal Dependencies (UD) treebanks, labels their licensing environments, and perturbs these into minimal pairs. Evaluating 12 multilingual and 2 monolingual models alongside n-gram baselines, we find that multilingual models struggle most with lower-resource languages and with pairs that are not n-gram solvable. We further examine the effects of NPI typology, language family, licensing variability, and NPI-licenser distance. Data: this https URL

### [60] [Training User Simulators with Latent Intrinsic Feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13617)
*Tarek Naous,Craig Boutilier,Wei Xu,Ofer Meshi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: User simulators are gaining attention as environments to train LLM assistants that can better cope with the nuances of multi-turn conversations with real users. Prior work on user simulation has emphasized generating realistic user utterances, leaving unexplored their potential as a source of direct feedback on the assistant's responses. Such evaluation signals may not be explicitly communicated in language, but can instead reside in the latent reasoning of users. In this work, we introduce user simulators with intrinsic feedback, namely, models equipped with latent evaluation states: internal thoughts, reactions, and scalar ratings that evaluate the assistant from a first-person user perspective at each conversation turn. We train LLM-based simulators using interaction logs between real users and assistants and demonstrate that intrinsic feedback improves simulation realism and critiquing behaviors versus prompted simulator baselines, while also providing turn-level evaluations that existing fine-tuned simulators lack. Further, evaluations generated by our trained simulators correlate better with human judgments than those of prompted simulators of the same size. Lastly, our experiments reveal that simulators with intrinsic feedback provide effective reward signals for multi-turn RL training, matching setups that rely on external judge LLMs for rewards while cutting RL compute by more than half.

### [61] [AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13627)
*Natapong Nitarach,Phume Ngampornsukswadi,Pittawat Taveekitworachai,Surapon Nonesung,Warit Sirichotedumrong,Kunat Pipatanakul*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) on AMLworld's smallest test splits is costly because each of over a million targets requires a separate graph prompt. Sampling reduces this cost, but small balanced subsets change unweighted precision and F1. We introduce AMLworld-Compact, an evaluation set that retains every illicit test transaction and samples benign transactions from supervised-score strata. Its HT-Coreset protocol reduces evaluation targets by 271x and 611x on HI-Small and LI-Small. Horvitz-Thompson weights give unbiased full-test confusion-count estimates for fixed predictions; recall is exact, while precision and F1 are ratio estimates. In a held-out study using Graph Feature Preprocessor (GFP) features, one boosted-tree family defines strata for evaluating the other over 500 draws per configuration. At the released sizes, F1 RMSE is 0.00-2.58 percentage points versus 4.44-7.41 for uniform sampling with HT weights; conservative intervals remain broad. Under the evaluated graph prompts, seven open-weight LLMs have weighted precision near the predict-all-illicit baseline. In an outcome-stratified audit of 1,000 HI-Small few-shot outputs from one run per model, lexical checks pass for 84.5% of correct and 56.2% of incorrect binary verdicts, so these markers do not establish correctness. We release the evaluation sets, construction code, and audit tools at this https URL and this https URL .

### [62] [Multi-Stream Attention Residuals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630)
*Xiaohan Qin,Xiangdong Zhang,Tuo Dai,Sunan Zou,Huaijin Wu,Yebin Yang,Zhuo Xia,Lin Yao,Yuliang Liu,Junchi Yan*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Attention Residuals (AttnRes) enables content-dependent retrieval over network depth, which can be viewed as single-stream softmax attention along the depth axis. Inspired by the success of multi-head attention along the sequence axis, we introduce Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR), an extension of AttnRes that generalizes this mechanism to multi-head depth attention, yielding substantial performance gains with minimal additional overhead. MSAR draws stream diversity from sequence context through multi-scale causal convolutions, allowing different heads to retrieve historical representations through distinct contextual views while preserving the integrity of the hidden representation. The retrieved streams are combined through lightweight adaptive mixing to generate the single-stream layer input. By retaining single-stream sources and expanding them on demand, MSAR supports multi-stream computation without requiring persistent multi-stream storage or communication. Across all 12 downstream benchmarks at the 18B and 28B MoE scales, MSAR consistently outperforms prior residual variants, including standard residual connections, manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), and AttnRes. Scaling-law experiments yield an iso-loss compute speedup of $1.58\times$ over the standard residual baseline, compared with $1.35\times$ for AttnRes and $1.30\times$ for mHC. These results make MSAR a promising residual architecture for large-scale pre-training.

### [63] [Retractions Revisited: A Replication, Extension, and Mechanistic Evaluation of Linguistic Obfuscation Effects in Fraudulent Science](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13678)
*David M. Markowitz*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Prior work suggests fraudulent scientists write their articles with higher rates of linguistic obfuscation than genuine scientists, with a possible mechanism suggesting obfuscation makes research more costly for a reader to analyze. This result has not undergone additional empirical scrutiny in the open science era, nor have other psychological mechanisms been evaluated. The current replication and extension addressed this opportunity by comparing 800 fraudulent and 800 genuine control papers (2013-2025). The results supported the linguistic obfuscation hypothesis, suggesting fraudulent papers were more obfuscated than genuine ones. A parallel mediation model evaluated three competing mechanisms, finding that reality monitoring, as measured through decreased rates of adjectives, best explained the link between fraudulent science and linguistic obfuscation. Cross-validated detection accuracy using obfuscation features (60.7%) and an elastic net of over 100 language dimensions (71.6%) were significantly greater than chance. Implications for scientific fraud and psychology of language research are discussed.

### [64] [Verifiable Retrieval for Legal Reasoning through Structure-driven Knowledge Graph](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13695)
*Ibrahim Siddig,Sviatoslav Tugeev,Munir Georges*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Any automation within reliability-critical contexts such as medicine or law has to be transparent and verifiable. Despite their advantages, current LLM-based systems do not meet these requirements due to their inherent black-box nature. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) attempts to ground the generative process in the relevant interpretable documents, thereby reducing the risk of AI 'hallucinations' and potentially enabling verification of the initial generation context. However, as the number and size of potential sources increases, naive retrieval approaches tend to perform worse, ignoring critical context elements. In this paper we aim to tackle this problem in the context of German Legal Code. Using structure-driven parsing to create a Knowledge Graph (KG) for the source document navigation and retrieval, we compare several KG-informed chunking and retrieval strategies and evaluate their effect on the accuracy of retrieved citations.

### [65] [Enhancing Legal Reasoning in Pre-trained Language Models via Knowledge Graph-Guided Multi-Task Pre-training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13722)
*Ibrahim Siddig,Munir Georges*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Legal language understanding requires reasoning over semi-structured regulatory documents, yet standard pre-training objectives do not explicitly target this structural capability. Because current legal language models rely solely on masked language modeling, they treat statutory text as flat token sequences and ignore the underlying hierarchical constraints. To bridge this gap, we present a multi-task pre-training approach for German traffic law (StVO). Our approach combines three complementary objectives: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP), Knowledge Graph (KG) Guided Clustering (CLU), and Knowledge Graph (KG) Aware Paragraph Classification (CLS). This approach explicitly encodes structured legal knowledge directly into the model weights. This encoding enables zero-shot legal reasoning at inference time and removes the need for discrete graph traversal. We evaluate our approach across nine Transformer-based encoders and 324 experimental runs. On synthetic StVO question answering, our models demonstrate consistent relative improvements between 10.3% and 155.0% over baselines. Furthermore, relative to the established LexGLUE baselines (Chalkidis et al., 2022), our models improve over prior results on four of seven legal benchmarks. It also achieves consistent zero-shot transfer gains between 3.4% and 15.8% on Austrian driving regulations. These experimental results indicate that our training approach generalizes successfully beyond the initial training legal domain.

### [66] [Not Just an Evaluation: A Case Study of Discourse Particle Sensitivity in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13794)
*William Sheffield,Jiahui Chen,Amy Zhang,Alex Warstadt,Junyi Jessy Li,Kanishka Misra*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Discourse particles subtly shape the flow of discourse by reflecting conversational context and interlocutor attitudes, often leaving the truth-conditional meaning untouched. They are also often polyfunctional, with distinct senses which partially overlap with other particles; for example, the exclusive use of English "just" and "only" ("John only/just drinks water"). Despite the frequency of these words in natural language, they have gone largely unstudied due to the subtle nature of their effects. We investigate LLM sensitivity to "just" and "only" in natural conversations using behavioral and mechanistic analyses. First, we find that LLMs and humans similarly prefer the presence of these particles in context, and both are more sensitive to "just" compared to "only". Second, when sampling from LLMs with and without these particles, we find LLMs consistently rate generations as more likely, given their source context, demonstrating their particle sensitivity. In both experiments, instruction tuning increases sensitivity. Finally, we localize particle-sensitive units within LLMs and find the overlap between "just" and "only" is asymmetric: "only" units transfer selectively to exclusive "just", while all "just" units transfer to "only" equally well regardless of sense, suggesting LLM lexical-level particle representations are partially organized by sense. We release our code, sense-labeled dialogue stimuli, and human preference annotations at this https URL .

### [67] [REFLECT: Role-Aware Detection of Sentiment, Emotion, Politeness, and Formality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13797)
*Sangpil Youm,Annabel Stocks Natalias,Hayden Heninger,Leah Jones,Xiaoyang Jin,Xiaoya Zhang,Bonnie Dorr*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Detecting communicative meaning in dialogue requires modeling not only lexical content but also the participant-role structures through which sentiment, emotion, politeness, and formality (SEPF) are expressed. Existing approaches rely on contextual language representations while leaving semantic roles implicit. We introduce a role-aware transformer architecture that maps the four SEPF dimensions to theory-grounded Semantic Role Labeling (SRL) configurations, incorporating these configurations directly into the transformer's self-attention mechanism. Role-aware attention models non-directional internal states (sentiment and emotion), while directional role-aware attention captures initiator-to-recipient relations for external cues (politeness and formality). The resulting role-aware representations are fused with contextual embeddings through a learned gate that adaptively weights how much role information each input contributes, rather than appending semantic roles as an auxiliary feature vector. Across four benchmark datasets, the framework yields statistically reliable gains over strong BERT-based baselines for emotion, politeness, and formality, with gains concentrated in theoretically predicted cases such as low-frequency, complex emotions and highly polite expressions; sentiment improvements are marginal and non-significant, suggesting that sentiment is conveyed more through lexical choice than participant-role structure. Additional evaluation on real-world data demonstrates that the framework improves both predictive performance and model traceability. These results demonstrate that linguistically grounded modifications to transformer self-attention improve the detection of communicative meaning, generalize beyond benchmark datasets to real-world mental-health data, and yield traceable, role-grounded explanations that extend beyond predictive performance to interpretability.

### [68] [Error Rate is Not Enough: Costs of Augmentation in Low-Resource ASR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13807)
*Katsumi Ibaraki,David Chiang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Data augmentation is standard practice for low-resource automatic speech recognition (ASR), but its benefits are almost always reported as aggregate error rates, leaving open why and when a method helps. On four low-resource languages and English at five data sizes, we cross two augmentations that modify existing audio (speed perturbation and SpecAugment) with two that modify text transcriptions and synthesize audio from it. We analyze errors at the phoneme level and find that they help for complementary reasons. SpecAugment has the most reliable aggregate improvements, but increases tone and palatalization errors, whereas text-based methods introduce consonant insertions; in combination, each reduces the errors the other introduces. This complementarity is predictable. Tone and palatalization are each signaled by a single acoustic property and occur least frequently in training (lowest training exposure), and text-based methods that flatten word frequency raise their frequency by 37--38%, reversing those errors while further improving aggregate error. The improvement from combining the methods exceeds the sum of their individual improvements; the superadditivity vanishes by 100 hours, limiting the complementarity to the low-resource regime. Where specific error types matter, we recommend selecting augmentation by training exposure and acoustic properties, both measurable before any training.

### [69] [Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13821)
*Juan Terven,Diana-Margarita Córdova-Esparza,Ruben Gomez,Carlos Miranda Rocha,Julio-Alejandro Romero-González,Edgar Chavez-Urbiola*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A useful language model should know when to answer and when to say "I don't know." Can we improve that decision by training the model itself or by training a separate component to check its answers? We study both approaches on Qwen3-14B for factual questions, using a score that rewards correct answers, penalizes mistakes, and allows abstention. Across three training seeds and two held-out confidence thresholds, a learned answer selector improves threshold-averaged utility over the original model's calibrated confidence filter. On TriviaQA, mean coverage increases from 20.2% to 30.9%, while the pooled error rate among scored answers decreases from 23.0% to 14.5% under exact-match grading. The tested reinforcement-learning changes do not establish consistent gains. On NQ-Open, the selector improves threshold-averaged utility over the filter but still performs worse than always abstaining. A partial human-reviewed audit preserves the TriviaQA finding. Our results support learning to select answers in this setting while showing that reliable abstention across datasets remains unresolved.

### [70] [Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13896)
*Xiao Zhang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Neural semantic parsers generate meaning representations token by token, yet well-formedness depends on references, scope, and graph relations that unfold during generation. Constrained decoding prevents locally invalid tokens but does not guarantee that a valid prefix can be completed within a fixed output-length limit. We investigate structural automata at three stages of DRS parsing (decoding, post hoc processing, and training) and additionally evaluate decoding on AMR. For decoding, we introduce accepting-path decoding (APD), which maintains a verified completion within the remaining length limit and follows the model's preferred token whenever that token can also be completed. APD guarantees an accepted output without retracting tokens. Under tight length limits, it improves Smatch++ over local masking by 5.1 and 2.4 points on DRS and by 6.4 and 3.2 points on AMR, comparable to rollback under the same limit, which retracts tokens. For post hoc processing, invalid outputs concentrate on the same inputs: eight unconstrained samples yield no valid output for 10.2% of inputs with limited training data, compared with 0.4% with full data, where filtering comes within 0.2 Smatch++ points of APD. For training, penalizing automaton-rejected tokens improves development Smatch++ by 3.6-11.0 points after 10% of training, but this advantage diminishes as cross-entropy alone reduces the probability assigned to rejected tokens from 14% to below 2% within the first sixth of training with limited data.

### [71] [When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13910)
*Shubh Garg,Chen Shani*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly analyze and reason about images, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations faithfully encode the structured relations required for such reasoning. We introduce EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), a metric for testing whether representations consistently encode concepts under controlled one-concept interventions, and CASP-VL (Causally controlled Spatial Perturbations for Vision-Language models), a benchmark of causally controlled spatial perturbations derived from Visual Genome scene graphs. Across multiple VLM architectures, we find that spatial relations are represented substantially less faithfully than lexical information, even when the same models score well above chance on compositional benchmarks. Further analysis shows that the relation is identifiable at the predicate's own tokens but is lost when the sentence is aggregated into a global representation, whether through the (EOS) token or by mean pooling. These findings reveal a systematic failure invisible to output-based evaluation: VLMs do not preserve, in the representation used downstream, relational information that is present in their own input.

### [72] [RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912)
*Taoyong Cui,Pinxian Zeng,Wanghan Xu,Hao Xiao,Shuhan Xue,Qiang Gao,Wanli Ouyang,Pheng Ann Heng,Zhenfei Yin,Yingcheng Wu,Ling Yang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) aims to transform interaction experience into persistent improvements, yet external feedback is costly and world-model predictions may become unreliable as policies evolve. We introduce RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework built on JEPA-Anything that uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection. Observed feedback drives policy or workflow improvement and conditional world-model adaptation, while component and compatibility checks govern the retention of updated policy-model pairs. Across diverse computational and scientific domains, RSI-Anything demonstrates substantial gains. In code repair, with the coder fixed, success increases from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% through predictive selection and 31.2% after world-model adaptation, at comparable test usage. Graphical user interface (GUI) evaluations showed higher task completion, while average actions decrease by 39.4%. Across five successive policy versions, laboratory-planning scores more than double from 21.80% to 46.01%. In reaction optimization, RSI-Anything achieves 96.15% mean best observed yield versus 82.16% for Bayesian optimization under the same 40-experiment budget. An end-to-end immune-science application further connects workflow evolution and predictive modeling with therapeutic hypothesis generation. These results demonstrate how predictive world models and retained system updates enable recursive improvement across diverse environments.

### [73] [Knowing Is Not Telling: Identity Ossification in LLM Representations of Trans-border Communities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12610)
*Minglu Sun,Lan Chen,Hang Jiang*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Ethnic and cultural identities rarely align with political borders, a tension made sharper by migration and long-standing cross-border ties. Communities such as the Sami, the Rohingya, and the Kurds have long lived across more than one state. This tension is especially clear in mainland Southeast Asia, where many communities share history, language, and culture across state lines. We study nine such transborder ethnic communities along China's southwestern border with mainland Southeast Asia, looking at how large language models (LLMs) represent them. We define and study identity ossification: a pattern where LLMs turn a fluid, cross-border ethnic identity into a single, fixed nation-state identity. We introduce the Transborder Identity Ossification Diagnostic Framework (TIODF) that compares direct factual questions with open-ended narrative questions to test whether ossification comes from missing knowledge or from how models frame their answers. We test GPT-5.1 and DeepSeek-V3.2 in English and Chinese. Ossification varies substantially across models and query languages. It appears in only 10.1% of GPT-5.1's English answers, but in 62.6% of DeepSeek-V3.2's Chinese answers. Models often still tell a single-nation story even when they answer the factual question correctly. This decoupling suggests that ossification reflects narrative framing rather than simple knowledge absence, which matters for how we test cultural fairness in multilingual AI systems.

### [74] [Large Language Models, Machine-Assisted Cultural Analytics, and the Agentic Turn](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12792)
*Andres Karjus*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Technologies like large language models make it easier to convert cultural material into analyzable variables, while LLM-driven agentic systems extend machine assistance to other parts of the research workflow. Rather than a full how-to guide or an exhaustive review of recent LLM use cases, this chapter looks at some crucial aspects of this new paradigm as well as the bigger picture. I argue that these technologies expand the scale, methodological range, and scope for delegation, while the basic logic by which those measurements support cultural claims remains mostly unchanged.

Rather than a full how-to guide or an exhaustive review of recent LLM use cases, this chapter looks at some crucial aspects of this new paradigm as well as the bigger picture. I argue that these technologies expand the scale, methodological range, and scope for delegation, while the basic logic by which those measurements support cultural claims remains mostly unchanged.

### [75] [What Counts as Evidence? Epistemic Cue Utilization in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12788)
*Jinchang Zhang,Kaijun Jiang,Guoyu Lu*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Which information actually shapes a language model's judgment when sources disagree? We study epistemic cue utilization through a controlled benchmark of 500 scenarios and five complementary tracks separating cue identification, cue influence, and competition between source, temporal, and presentation cues. Across 13 LLMs, nearly identical recognition of relative source reliability can accompany effects ranging from negligible to complete choice reversal when source histories are exchanged. The resulting profiles distinguish models that rely on source history from those more responsive to evidence lineage, event time, or presentation order. We then intervene on three Qwen checkpoints using matched sham material, fact restatement, structured evidence records, and an additional weighting principle. Restatement increases reliability sensitivity in the two 27B models, and adding the principle increases it by a further 39.2 and 47.2 percentage points relative to the ledger. The 9B model instead changes its sensitivity to evidence lineage without a comparable reliability response. Verified-state accuracy remains 100\% throughout these interventions. Together, the benchmark and interventions show that identifying an epistemic cue and allowing it to influence judgment are distinct, experimentally measurable aspects of model behavior.

### [76] [Developing Competency in AI Ethics: A training framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13319)
*Alexandra Prégent,Alexei Grinbaum*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: We present a training framework for developing core competencies in the practical operationalisation of AI ethics: (1) identifying ethical concerns; (2) determining which standard ethics requirements they implicate; (3) selecting and prioritising concrete technical and organisational measures to address them; and (4) recognising ethics tensions and reasoning about trade-offs where such tensions cannot be fully resolved. The framework is intended for researchers and engineers in AI, Research Ethics Committee members, policymakers, and students, providing them with practical tools for translating abstract ethical requirements into concrete actions. The framework provides a step-by-step approach organised around four interconnected tasks: issue identification, requirement mapping, measure selection, and tension identification. These tasks are supported by a suite of training materials, including an Ethics Checklist and a Portfolio of Measures. Here, we complement them with a set of practical exercises of three different types as well as trainer guides. We also discuss lessons learned in pilot training sessions and offer recommendations for trainers.

### [77] [Who Can Say No? Control, Accountability and the Pace of Frontier AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13340)
*Rikard Rosenbacke,Carl Rosenbacke,Victor Rosenbacke,Martin McKee*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: In September 2026, the leaders of the largest frontier AI laboratories said in public that the pace of capability improvement is too fast and that none of them can slow down alone, and agents under evaluation at OpenAI broke out of their test environment and reached a third party's live systems, which a UN-mandated panel called an early warning of one route to loss of human control. This paper examines the institutional side of that risk: not the machine, but the person who must control it. We argue that control is not taken by AI but given away, one delegation at a time, by organisations arranged so that nobody is positioned to say no, and we define control as a person who can detect a serious problem, challenge the decision, stop the system and reverse it, and who has something to lose by not doing so. Three questions follow, which any builder, funder, regulator or deployer can answer in public: (1) who inside the organisation can say no, and who answers for saying yes; (2) who outside the organisation checks the decision, and what can they do when they disagree; (3) what happens when AI builds AI faster than anyone can check it. A checkable answer needs a named person, a date, a number, and a stop that has been used or tested. Three measures meet that test: a named person on every consequential decision, including the standing instructions AI agents carry out; a supervisor with a stop authority; and two published clocks, time to build against time to check. We show that governance theory arrives at the same conditions, and code fifty older mechanisms against the questions, finding that almost every one began as one rule at one point, taken by one party without waiting for the rest. That is the paper's design: a start, not a solution. Publication is the first step and one laboratory can take it alone; the contract, the independent body and the law come after.

### [78] [Adversarial Attacks Reveal Divergent Deception Competence in Humans and Generative Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13363)
*Lucca Pfründer,Riccardo Loconte,Bruno Verschuere,Bennett Kleinberg*

Main category: cs.CY

TL;DR: Machine learning models typically outperform humans in deception detection. A threat to machine learning models is their vulnerability to adversarial attacks: subtle yet targeted perturbations of input data that trick a model into misclassification. Yet, this also provides an opportunity: understanding how humans versus machines construct attacks offers new insights into second-order beliefs about deception. In a preregistered experiment (n = 501), we compare the effectiveness, efficiency, and nature of a paraphrasing attack by humans and generative language models on an automated deception classifier. We find that humans were more effective attackers when rewriting truthful statements to be deceptive, while the generative language model was more effective and efficient at making lies sound like truths. Computational text analysis suggests that this is because humans make targeted use of deception cues, while generative language models, instead, apply generic changes that signal truth. The failure to mimic deception is two-sided: while it exposes a blind spot in the machines increasingly used to detect lies, it also means that language models might facilitate successful lying.

### [79] [Distributed Datalog at Scale with Worst-Case Optimal Joins](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12692)
*Kunting Qi,Yihao Sun,Kristopher Micinski,Thomas Gilray,Sidharth Kumar*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: 本文提出了首个基于最坏情况最优连接（WCOJ）的分布式内存Datalog引擎，用于在无共享HPC集群上执行递归不动点评估。该引擎将Hypercube分区从单轮洗牌扩展到迭代半朴素求值，仅对每轮新推导的元组进行重新分区和复制，从而保持WCOJ交集始终在本地。在Aurora和Polaris超级计算机上的实验表明，系统在大多数基准测试中优于现有Datalog引擎。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 大规模关系推理（如社交网络分析、知识图谱推理、程序分析等）通常由循环多路连接主导。传统分布式Datalog系统依赖二元连接链，导致中间结果爆炸式增长，在递归场景下需要反复物化和重分配这些庞大的中间关系，造成严重的通信瓶颈。现有的WCOJ实现仅针对共享内存或一次性非递归查询，无法满足分布式HPC系统上递归评估的需求。

Method: 1. 基于Hypercube分区：选定一组连接变量作为分区键，定义k维逻辑进程网格；关系沿其包含的变量维度进行哈希分区，沿缺失维度进行复制。2. MPI实现：使用MPI_Alltoall+MPI_Alltoallv进行全局重分布，使用MPI_Allgather+MPI_Allgatherv在子立方体通信子中沿缺失维度复制。3. 迭代半朴素求值：每轮仅对新推导的delta元组执行重分布和复制，复用同一分区布局，保证所有WCOJ交集保持rank-local。4. 支持1D/2D/3D分区维度，提供了复制开销的代价模型。

Result: 在Polaris和Aurora超级计算机上使用图挖掘（Peer Influence、Triangle、TC、SG）和程序分析（Andersen指向分析）基准测试评估。从32扩展到2,048进程时，Polaris上最高获得14.3×加速比，Aurora上最高13.4×。在单节点32路并行下，在多数递归和循环基准测试中优于Soufflé、FlowLog和DuckDB。在分布式对比中，TC(USRoad)上比Slog快8.9–11.2×。2D分区在内存允许时运行时最优，3D分区在内存不可行时仍可运行但通信开销更大。

Conclusion: 该工作证明了WCOJ在HPC规模上的实用性，为可扩展图分析、程序分析和神经符号AI奠定了新基础。未来工作包括：用优化的非均匀all-to-all算法替代默认MPI_Alltoallv；集成机器学习驱动的自动调优器；基于代价的分区键和维度选择；偏斜感知的自适应复制；以及与GPU加速的本地连接相结合。

Abstract: Scalable logic-based analytics are frequently dominated by cyclic multi-way joins over large relational datasets. State-of-the-art systems evaluate these joins through chains of binary joins, incurring substantial overhead from large intermediate relations that must be materialized and redistributed across the network. Worst-Case Optimal Joins (WCOJ) offer a provably superior alternative by evaluating joins one variable at a time, eliminating intermediate blowup. However, existing WCOJ implementations target either shared-memory machines or one-shot, non-recursive queries on dataflow and big-data platforms, leaving WCOJ-based recursive evaluation on distributed-memory HPC systems an open problem. We present, to our knowledge, the first distributed-memory Datalog engine that uses WCOJ for recursive fixpoint evaluation. Our design builds on HyperCube partitioning, which hash-partitions relations along variable-aligned grid dimensions and replicates them along missing dimensions, and extends it from a single shuffle to iterative execution: in every semi-naive iteration, only newly derived tuples are repartitioned and re-replicated, using MPI all-to-all collectives and per-dimension all-gathers over subcube communicators, while the same layout is reused across iterations so that all WCOJ intersections remain rank-local. We evaluate our system on the Aurora and Polaris leadership-class supercomputers at Argonne National Laboratory using graph mining and program analysis benchmarks, demonstrating strong scalability, outperforming state-of-the-art Datalog engines on most benchmarks, and characterizing how partition dimensionality trades runtime against memory feasibility.

</details>


### [80] [Semantic Views: Certified Reuse of LLM Labels Across Semantic Queries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12768)
*Oktie Hassanzadeh,Dharmashankar Subramanian*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: SemViews提出了一种认证式语义过滤器，通过重用历史查询的LLM标签（语义视图）、嵌入和辅助模型分数来排序元组，仅用新鲜分层oracle样本进行认证，从而在保证精度和召回率（至少1-δ概率）的前提下，减少28%-45%的oracle调用。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 语义查询引擎中每次LLM评估都是昂贵的oracle调用，现有优化方法（如级联、有限样本保证方法）存在权衡困境：信任廉价代理的级联方法常无法满足精度召回目标，有限样本保证方法节省调用有限，且所有方法都丢弃了查询结束时的oracle标签。不同谓词之间的标签重用存在安全风险，相似性缓存和蕴含关系重用因统计包含而非逻辑包含而频繁失败。

Method: SemViews的核心是CertifiedFilter算子，分五个步骤：(1)匹配最相似的k=10个候选视图；(2)在200个元组的shaping样本上拟合L2正则化逻辑回归分数模型，特征包括视图标签指示符、辅助模型分数和32维局部嵌入；(3)在分数边界附近细化分数（最多8轮，每轮标记5%元组）；(4)规划器将元组分为拒绝区X、oracle区O和接受区A，最小化预测调用数；(5)用无放回分层抽样从X和A中抽取认证样本，使用精确超几何边界，结合δ分割（f∈{0.5,0.7,0.9}）进行认证。视图仅用于规划order，oracle样本仅用于决定真伪。

Result: 在四个数据集（PubMed、GoEmotions、DBpedia、Reviews，共725,000条记录oracle标签）上，SemViews在99.63%的查询中满足精度和召回目标，节省28%-45%的oracle调用，而唯一具有相同保证的先前方法BARGAIN需要1.32x-1.71x的调用。视图在相关谓词上额外节省11%-38%调用，在改写问题上节省27%-36%。所有更便宜的方法（相似性缓存、SemWeave、级联）至少在32.4%的查询上未达目标。在10万级关系上的扩展实验证实效率随表规模提升（DBpedia从60%降至34%）。

Conclusion: SemViews证明了语义过滤器可以同时获得认证和低成本：通过将free side information用于排序、将新鲜样本用于认证，可以安全地跨查询重用oracle标签。视图帮助程度与工作负载中谓词相关性成正比，在改写问题上效果最显著，而未经认证的重用（相似性或蕴含）在大量查询上失败。更广泛的启示是，允许side information塑造计划而仅让fresh samples进入边界，可使语义引擎在不冒险保证的情况下利用任何积累的知识。

Abstract: Semantic query engines evaluate natural-language filters with a large language model, and every evaluation is a costly oracle call. Optimizers that reduce these calls face a dilemma: cascades that trust a cheap proxy miss their precision and recall targets on many queries, methods with finite-sample guarantees save little, and all of them discard the oracle's labels when the query ends. We present SemViews, a certified semantic filter that orders tuples by signals that cost no oracle calls (the labels that earlier queries left behind as semantic views, a local embedding, and a helper model's score), refines that order with labels it must pay for anyway, and certifies its answer with fresh stratified oracle samples. The answer meets user precision and recall targets with probability at least $1-\delta$ for every workload and every catalog, so a stale or misleading view can cost oracle calls but never accuracy. On four workloads replayed against 725,000 recorded oracle labels, SemViews meets both targets on 99.63% of queries and saves 28%-45% of the oracle calls, whereas the only prior method in our study with the same guarantee needs 1.32x-1.71x as many calls. When a question returns in different words, views cut its calls by a further 27%-36%, with both targets met on at least 99.8% of such queries; similarity caches and entailment-based reuse meet them on only 17%-47%.

</details>


### [81] [CALQA: Conformal Screening of Forecast-Ensemble Configurations from One Mergeable State](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13249)
*Xiufeng Liu,Ruyu Liu,Yusen Liu,Huan Huo,Per Sieverts Nielsen*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: CALQA是一个可合并、可删除的整数聚合状态，用于在权重网格上对分位数平均（Vincentized）集成做保形校准筛选。它无需逐行扫描即可对任意权重向量打分，并通过两阶段搜索（粗筛+精确复核前100名）在604个公开面板组（10⁴候选/组）上达到精确搜索持有方块得分的99.95%，加速1.3–59倍；在约10⁸行的两个真实面板（智能电表、零售销售）上加速44–54倍，持有方块得分达99.98–100.01%，且在相同字节预算下优于块样本筛选。该聚合在保形覆盖保证下被严格证明为渐近最优，但在小/贪心搜索或K=12全支撑场景下不具优势。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: AutoML系统为每个分组/时段搜索大量集成权重向量以寻找最窄的保形校准区间；精确校准需逐行扫描，对G组×M候选计算开销达GM次扫描，亟需一种无需读行即可安全筛选的近似方法。

Method: 固定网格N上每个净点存储分箱直方图的状态；通过GROUP BY扩展、减法删除、窗格加权支持合并与回滚；查询时对每个候选w返回min_m(t_m + ½‖w−w_m‖₁)，其中t_m为围点阈值；两阶段计划先用状态粗筛全部候选，再对前k名做精确重检；理论证明其夹逼精确分位移位并转移Barber等人的加权保形覆盖界至每个事后权重向量。

Result: 在5个公开面板604组、10⁴候选下，两阶段（k=100）持有方块Winkler得分达精确搜索的99.95%，加速1.3–59倍，状态单独为100.41%；在约10⁸行的CER智能电表与M5零售面板上加速44–54倍，得分达99.98–100.01%，且在相同字节下优于块样本筛选（遗憾0.25–0.65% vs 1.43–1.88%）；状态内存为|N|(J+1)+1个整数（K=4时约21KB），在DUckDB中筛选比精确SQL快13–2301倍。

Conclusion: CALQA将保形校准转化为可合并、可删除的数据库聚合，作为筛选器匹配精确搜索质量但耗时大幅降低；其大小在其类别内达到渐近最优（Θ_d(Bε^{−(1+d)})），但在小/贪心搜索、充足内存下网外权重或K=12全支撑时无优势；开放问题包括漂移下自适应重校准、一般状态下界与净直方图下界之间的指数缺口、以及随机化摘要。

Abstract: AutoML systems fit ensemble weights over model libraries; a search can score, per category, market or time pane, thousands of weightings of the quantile-averaged (Vincentized) ensemble for the narrowest conformally calibrated interval; exact calibration scores a group's rows per candidate. We present CALQA, a fixed-size integer aggregate per group and pane that stores histograms of normalised block scores at a net of weight vectors. One GROUP BY builds it; it merges by addition, retracts deletions by subtraction and scores any candidate without reading a row. We prove that its score never falls below the exact split-conformal shift and exceeds it by at most the net distance plus a grid gap; that coverage carries over to each fixed weight vector and, for i.i.d. blocks and up to a union-bound slack, to a searched weight vector deployed with the state's shift; and how small any such state can be. The state is thus a screen: it ranks all candidates, and exact recomputation re-checks the top 100. On five public panels (604 groups, 10,000 candidates each) this two-stage plan matches exact search on held-out blocks (99.95% of its Winkler score), 1.3-59 times faster. On two real panels of about $10^8$ rows (smart meters, retail sales) it is 44-54 times faster at 99.98-100.01% of that score and beats sample screens with the same re-check in regret at less total time. Picks deployed with their exact shift need a held-out coverage check. The state does not pay off for small or greedy searches, off-net weights at ample memory or full twelve-member support.

</details>


### [82] [MatQuery: Execution-Grounded Natural-Language Querying over Heterogeneous Materials Databases](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13573)
*Chen Jason Zhang,Qi Chen*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: MatQuery是一个用于跨多个异构材料数据库的自然语言查询原型与实验基础设施，通过"语言模型提议+程序步骤检查"的八步流水线，在冻结的六个公共材料数据库本地副本上生成、执行并组装查询，配套有基准生成器与评估框架。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 材料科学家常需跨多个公共材料数据库（如Materials Project、OQMD、AFLOW、JARVIS-DFT、NOMAD、COD）联合检索，但各库schema、字段命名、单位、计算约定各异；现有NL-to-SQL系统（如CHESS、Alpha-SQL）和单库材料代理（如LLaMP、ChatMOF）均未解决跨库异构、科学含义依赖方法约定、以及"执行成功≠可比较"这三个核心问题。

Method: 构建冻结的、自验证的六库本地副本（每库约10,000条记录），建立统一的字段目录与数据库无关的中间查询表示（及每库适配器）；设计八步流水线（字段表→条件提取→逐库字段链接→源选择→规范查询编译→带反馈执行→选择合并算子→结果对账装配），其中模型调用负责"提议"，确定性程序步骤负责"检查/执行/装配"；基准生成器采用"先生成可执行参考查询，再由模型措辞问题，并经回译与评审把关"；评估框架对直接提示、CHESS、Alpha-SQL在同一冻结基础上做执行准确率与源选择准确率比较。

Result: 在800题开发集上：直接生成+3个示例的严格执行准确率达82.4%（无示例56.5%），执行成功率84.4%；低成本源打分器在完整请求上达到85.0%的精确库集合选择（单决策ROC AUC=0.995，校准后ECE=0.0125，5,520次决策成本仅0.032美元）；按组分聚类的跨库审计显示31.6%的带隙差异>0.5 eV；50次澄清会话试点中probe-then-ask策略仅11/50被双评审判为有效，未达预设门槛；300对结构审计中仅115对能完成结构比对，组分链接的设计加权精度约33.1%（部分识别区间8.5–82.8%）。完整流水线尚处冒烟测试阶段，未进行大规模评估。

Conclusion: 跨库材料查询可在相当比例上被转换为与参考答案执行一致的查询，但这只证明查询正确而非科学可比；按组分聚类时数值分歧普遍且组分链接不可靠，身份判定必须依靠结构匹配；简单的probe-and-ask设计因生成路径脆弱且问题针对性差而失败；当前结果仅反映开发集与试点行为，完整流水线的规模化评估以及独立专家评审仍待进行。

Abstract: Materials scientists increasingly combine information from several public databases, each with its own interface, schema, units and calculation conventions. MatQuery is a prototype and experimental infrastructure for studying how a natural-language request can be turned into queries over such databases and how the returned values can be interpreted. This report describes what has been built and the preliminary results obtained so far. The prototype holds frozen, self-verifying local copies of six public materials databases (about 10,000 records each), a catalog of declared fields derived from them, a database-independent query representation with an adapter for each database, and an eight-step pipeline in which a language model proposes and deterministic program steps check, execute and assemble. A benchmark generator produces questions whose reference queries are verified by execution on the frozen copies and whose wording is checked by back-translation and review. An evaluation harness runs direct prompting, CHESS and Alpha-SQL on the same frozen basis. Preliminary experiments on an 800-question development set show that direct generation with three demonstrations reaches 82.4% strict execution accuracy (56.5% without demonstrations), that a low-cost scorer selects the exact set of databases for 85.0% of complete requests with well-calibrated probabilities, and that band gaps differ by more than 0.5 eV in 31.6% of composition-matched cross-database clusters. Two pilots show the limits of the current approach: a probe-then-ask policy gave answers rated valid by both reviewers in only 11 of 50 sessions, and only 115 of 300 sampled record pairs could be compared by structure. The complete pipeline is in smoke testing and has not yet been evaluated at scale.

</details>


### [83] [Time-Varying Favorite-Longshot Bias in Polymarket Weather Markets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13593)
*Shouchen Qiu,Huaijun Qiu*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: 该论文研究Polymarket每日最高气温市场中"冷门-热门"偏差(favorite-longshot bias)随时间变化的特征,发现热门端在临近结算时存在显著高估,而冷门端高估主要出现在远期。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 先前跨类别研究表明Polymarket气象市场存在较大定价偏差,但未区分低价冷门与高价热门,也无法揭示偏差随结算临近的演变。本文旨在回答:冷门与热门偏差如何随时间变化,哪一端是气象市场主要错误来源。

Method: 利用10个城市、2189个事件、21697个合约、854万笔交易数据,按结算前48至1小时分为11个时间窗口。方法包括:(1)可靠性图分析;(2)区间偏差D_h(a,b)=mean(y-p),分别定义冷门(0<p≤0.10)与热门(0.75≤p≤0.95);(3)事件级Brier、Log Loss、RPS评分;(4)三次B样条logit重校准(两个内部节点);(5)Buy-NO交易测试,以$10名义价值计算含/不含费用收益,采用事件级bootstrap置信区间。

Result: 核心发现:(1)冷门高估集中在30-48小时远期,临近时减弱甚至转轻微低估;热门高估在最后1-12小时显著增强,事件加权偏差约-0.10(6小时),量级几乎是冷门偏差(-0.009,48小时)的十倍。(2)三种事件级评分在临近峰值时均改善,RPS降幅最大;B样条重校准虽点估计略好,但95%置信区间包含零,无统计显著改善。(3)Buy-NO测试:热门窗口后期费ROI达+50.71%(NO胜率20.7%),置信区间[1.76,102.98]¢;冷门窗口后期费ROI为-0.23%(NO胜率97.8%),置信区间包含零。事件加权与城市等权结果一致,表明非个别城市驱动。

Conclusion: 气象市场的冷门-热门偏差具有强烈的时间不对称性:冷门偏差为远期现象且较温和,热门偏差为临近结算时主导错误来源,量级大一个数量级。整体分布精度在临近时仍提升,说明热门偏差局限在较小的高价子集中。B样条重校准因聚合了所有桶而无法显著改善分数。Buy-NO对比进一步验证热门端高估具有经济一致性且效应更大。局限在于仅覆盖每日最高气温、十个城市及一个月测试期,未来将与公共概率天气预报对比。

Abstract: Prediction-market prices combine traders' judgments about future outcomes, but their errors may be concentrated in particular price ranges and change as settlement approaches. Prior cross-category evidence shows that Polymarket weather markets have larger pricing bias than other major categories, without separating low-price longshots from high-price favorites. This study compares the two ranges at different horizons in daily maximum-temperature markets. Event-level probability scores, cubic B-spline recalibration, and Buy-NO tests are used to examine the form and effect of the bias. Longshot overpricing mainly occurs at distant horizons, whereas favorite overpricing becomes much stronger during the final 1-12 hours and is nearly one order of magnitude larger. Event-level scores improve toward the daily temperature peak, while simple recalibration yields no statistically significant gains. The Buy-NO results in the corresponding time windows also show that the main pricing error is concentrated at the favorite end.

</details>


### [84] [Benchmarking Content-Defined Chunking Algorithms for Data Deduplication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13704)
*Marcel Gregoriadis,Leonhard Balduf,Björn Scheuermann,Johan Pouwelse*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: 该论文系统评估了八种基于内容定义分块（CDC）的基础分块算法，在四种真实工作负载下从吞吐量、去重率、平均块大小和块大小方差四个维度进行分析。同时修正了AE算法参数化中长期存在的错误。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有的数据去重基准测试将基础分块算法和高层技术（如大小归一化、最小/最大阈值、缓存）混为一谈，导致无法识别哪些设计选择真正影响性能。作者旨在解耦这些层次，单独评估基础分块算法，并纠正AE算法参数化中的一个长期错误。

Method: 将CDC算法分解为模块化结构，隔离出基础分块算法层；在四种真实工作负载下评估八种先进基础分块算法；通过吞吐量、去重率、平均块大小和块大小方差四个指标进行衡量；推导出AE、RAM、MII算法参数与期望块大小之间关系的新公式。

Result: 1) 发现AE参数化中存在长期错误，导致生成的块比预期小13-39%，并夸大了其报告的去重率；2) AE是四种指标综合表现最均衡的基础分块算法；3) RAM与AE的相似性在低熵数据上不成立；4) 在面向存储的工作负载中，MII和PCI相对于更简单的替代方案的优势有限。

Conclusion: AE是综合性能最均衡的基础分块算法，但对参数化的修正至关重要；简单的算法在存储工作负载中可能与复杂算法表现相当；该研究强调了对CDC算法进行模块化评估的重要性，并开源了所有实现、数据集和分析脚本以促进可复现性。

Abstract: Data deduplication relies on content-defined chunking (CDC) algorithms to decide where data is split. We observe that most CDC algorithms are modular: a base chunking algorithm fixes the byte-level cut-point condition, while high-level techniques (size normalization, min/max thresholds, caching) layer on top. Existing benchmarks conflate the two, obscuring which design choices actually drive performance. We isolate and evaluate eight state-of-the-art base chunking algorithms across four realistic workloads and four metrics: throughput, deduplication ratio, mean chunk size, and chunk-size variance. Further, we derive new formulas relating algorithm parameters to expected chunk size for AE, RAM, and MII. In doing so, we uncover a longstanding error in the widely-used AE parameterization reproduced across multiple papers and evaluation tools that produces chunks 13-39% smaller than intended and inflates AE's reported deduplication. Across our evaluation, AE is the most balanced base chunking algorithm across all four metrics, RAM's similarity to AE does not carry over to low-entropy data, and MII and PCI show limited advantages over simpler alternatives in storage-oriented workloads. We release all implementations, datasets, and analysis scripts as open source.

</details>


### [85] [ProvQML: Efficient Provenance Capture for Machine Learning as Recursive Aggregate SQL [Extended Version]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13756)
*Nkechi J. Akinwale,Seokki Lee*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: ProvQML是一个基于Apache Spark的递归聚合SQL引擎，通过将ML算法表达为递归聚合SQL查询，高效捕获细粒度的数据来源（provenance），包括局部provenance（每个训练实例对梯度计算的贡献）和全局provenance（模型参数在迭代间的更新序列），以支持ML模型的可解释性。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有系统不支持对递归聚合SQL（用于表达ML算法）进行可扩展的provenance捕获，而ML可解释性（如模型验证、调试、特征重要性计算）需要这种细粒度的来源追踪能力。

Method: 1. 将ML查询中复杂的互递归和非线性递归关系通过查询重写（检测+重写两阶段）折叠为标准线性递归；2. 在递归case中使用窗口函数和子查询链（recProv→predProv→Grad）计算并物化局部provenance（Pred_i, Grad_i, Grad）；3. 基于PreM和PCC属性保证重写的语义正确性；4. 优化策略：广播小模型delta关系消除join shuffle、预分区训练数据按I减少reshuffle、delta-based计算将全局provenance内存控制在O(|T|)；5. 在Spark上实现ProvQML引擎。

Result: 在Income、BikeSharing、SpamBase、WebSpam四个真实数据集上，测试了5种ML算法（线性/Lasso/Ridge/Logistic回归、SVM）。端到端运行时随数据规模近似次线性增长；shuffle优化带来最高3.4倍加速；相比Radlog（不捕获provenance），provenance捕获开销最多约5倍；成功在分布式集群上处理WebSpam（138维特征、29M元组）和Income（17M元组）的大规模训练。

Conclusion: ProvQML证明了通过查询重写和优化技术，可以在线捕获ML训练过程的细粒度provenance（局部和全局），且开销可控，为ML模型可解释性、审计、特征贡献分析提供了声明式SQL基础。未来方向包括：provenance摘要技术、神经网络等更复杂ML算法、基于捕获provenance计算Shapley值等新解释。

Abstract: Expressing ML algorithms as recursive aggregate SQL queries over distributed systems enables large-scale declarative data analytics, yet no existing system supports scalable provenance capture, necessary for ML explainability. We present ProvQML, a provenance-aware recursive aggregate SQL engine that efficiently captures fine-grained provenance while evaluating ML algorithms as recursive aggregate queries. We capture two types of provenance: (i) local provenance that records the contribution of each training instance to gradient computation at a specific model state, and (ii) global provenance that encodes the sequence of model parameter updates across the iterations. Extensive experiments on widely used ML datasets demonstrate that our approach efficiently captures both provenance for various ML models over widely used ML datasets.

</details>


### [86] [Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13823)
*Oktie Hassanzadeh,Dharmashankar Subramanian*

Main category: cs.DB

TL;DR: This paper reveals that semantic query engines (using LLMs to evaluate rows) are not reproducible even at temperature 0. Through 1.2 million logged model calls across SemBench, LRO-Bench, and UDA-Bench, the authors show that 0.07%–10.2% of row-level operator outputs change across executions, and that query plans amplify these changes exponentially—turning a few percent of item changes into most answers changing. About 21% of published benchmark quality results change between executions, and 16 of 28 LRO-Bench implementation recommendations are not statistically settled. The changes concentrate on "contested" items where models disagree with each other, and are predictable from a single execution's decision margin or reasoning length. The authors propose reporting rules for benchmarks and design rules for engines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Semantic query engines increasingly rely on LLMs as oracles for filtering, mapping, joining, and aggregating rows. Benchmarks assume these oracles are reproducible at temperature 0, treating an execution as a property of the system. However, the LLM endpoints used in practice (hosted APIs and even open-weight deployments) exhibit output variation at temperature 0 due to dynamic batching, floating-point non-associativity, deployment changes, and other factors. The motivation is to quantify what this variance means for query processing—how many outputs change, whether changes survive relational operators, whether benchmark conclusions remain valid, and what causes the changes.

Method: The authors conduct an experimental study using three benchmarks (SemBench, LRO-Bench, UDA-Bench) run through their own harnesses at temperature 0. They log 1.2 million model calls across 8 deployments (6 open-weight models including gpt-oss-120B, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B, Mistral-Small-3.1-24B, Granite-3.3-8B; plus GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 5). They develop a possible-worlds probabilistic model that predicts answer reproduction from item-level disagreement distributions and the plan's shape. They measure item flip rates, answer reproduction, quality ranges, decision margins, and reasoning lengths. They also replay voting strategies and calibrated cascade algorithms on recorded outputs without new model calls, and probe causes (temperature control, seeds, concurrency, input order, reasoning effort, deployments).

Result: Key results: (1) Item flip rates span 0.07% to 10.2% over 5 executions at temperature 0 (up to 24% on one task); commercial models also vary. (2) Plans amplify item changes exponentially in the number of items an answer exposes—e.g., on UDA-Bench, a few percent of extracted values change but about two-thirds of SQL answers change. (3) 21% of SemBench's published quality results change between executions, including on deterministic plans; 16 of 28 LRO-Bench implementation recommendations are not statistically settled. (4) Changing items are contested across models (77% of changing items vs. 34% of stable items); identical requests within one execution disagree as often as across executions; one execution's decision margin or reasoning length predicts later changes (AUC up to 1.00). (5) Deployments matter: same model on different stacks returns different answers and variance profiles, and one deployment shifted between campaigns. (6) Voting reduces variance but cannot remove it because changes concentrate on items near decision boundaries; re-asking items flagged by reasoning length achieves most of a full vote's benefit at lower cost. (7) Calibrated cascades keep their statistical guarantees but which rows they return depends on which oracle execution labeled the sample. (8) Recording operator outputs (~39 bytes each) is the remedy that makes an answer reproducible.

Conclusion: The authors conclude that temperature 0 does not make a semantic query reproducible. Item-level changes propagate through query plans in ways predicted by a possible-worlds model, and benchmarks must report quality spreads, answer reproduction, and failure rates rather than single-execution numbers. They provide concrete reporting rules for benchmark designers (per-query quality with spread, answer reproduction, flip rates at stated k, no best-of-N reporting, record per-item outputs, report deployments, only state recommendations that hold across executions) and design rules for engine builders (treat stored semantic columns as one sample from a distribution with its margin; estimate answer stability from item disagreement and plan shape; calibrate optimizers on multiple executions and record labels; record operator outputs to make answers reproducible).

Abstract: Semantic query engines ask a large language model (LLM) to judge individual rows, and benchmarks compare these engines on the quality of a few executions at temperature 0. We measure how much another execution changes. We re-execute the text and tabular workloads of SemBench, LRO-Bench, and UDA-Bench through their own harnesses, log every one of 1.2 million model calls, and reanalyze SemBench's published executions. At temperature 0, between 0.07% and 10.2% of rows change their operator output over five executions, depending on the model, and up to 24.0% on one task. Plans amplify these changes exponentially in the number of rows an answer exposes, as a possible-worlds model predicts: on UDA-Bench, a few percent of extracted values change, but about two thirds of the answers do. In SemBench's published results, 21% of text results change quality between executions, including on engines whose plans are deterministic. Several per-query system comparisons, and 16 of 28 tests of LRO-Bench's implementation recommendations, are not settled by the executions the benchmarks run. Changing rows are rows on which models disagree with each other; identical requests within one execution disagree as often as across executions; and one execution's decision margin or reasoning length predicts which rows change. Voting reduces the variance but does not remove it, and a calibrated cascade keeps its guarantee while the rows it returns change. We derive reporting rules for benchmarks and design rules for engines.

</details>
