### [363] [Inference-Time Steering Across Scaffolds and Epitopes for Sample-Efficient De Novo Nanobody Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13844)
*Mason Minot,Simon Friedensohn,Cédric R. Weber*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Generative molecular design typically relies on over-generation and post-hoc filtering. Inference-time steering methods like Feynman-Kac (FK) steering improve efficiency by biasing trajectories toward high-reward candidates, yet they optimize within a single fixed configuration. In de novo nanobody design, upfront commitment to conditioning choices like scaffold identity or target epitope creates a bottleneck. Since yield varies across these conditions, steering unpromising setups wastes compute. We recast generative condition selection as an inference-time resource-allocation problem. We propose two dynamic budget allocators: a joint Global Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) formulation that steers and allocates compute across configurations concurrently, and a decoupled approach adapting Batched Successive Elimination (BaSE). Empirically, these dynamic allocators increase the yield of designable candidates per GPU-hour nearly 5$\times$ without sacrificing diversity across distinct therapeutic targets and generative configurations.

### [364] [Partially Informed Stochastic Optimization via Zeroth-Order Residual Tracking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13871)
*El Mahdi Chayti,Alireza Mirrokni,Martin Jaggi*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Many optimization problems provide direct access to only part of the gradient, while the remaining component must be inferred from function evaluations. This structure arises in performative prediction, performative reinforcement learning, and bilevel optimization with a black-box lower level. We introduce Partially Informed Stochastic Optimization (PISO), which combines the available gradient component with a running estimate of the residual. By centring each zeroth-order observation on this estimate, PISO makes the variance due to random probing depend on the tracking error rather than the residual's magnitude. This yields a randomized sketch iteration with an explicit contraction mechanism and a principled interpretation of momentum. For smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish convergence guarantees that depend on the residual's variation and initial magnitude, without requiring a uniform bound on the unavailable gradient component. With independently sampled function evaluations and Gaussian or spherical probes, PISO attains leading function-evaluation complexities of \(O(d^{2}\varepsilon^{-6})\) under Lipschitz gradients and \(O(d^{2}\varepsilon^{-5})\) under an additional Lipschitz-Hessian assumption. These rates require only one probe direction, two function samples, and one known-component sample per update. The analysis also quantifies how batching trades observations for fewer deployments. Across five settings, PISO variants improve on the tested baselines with comparable oracle access in three, reach a comparable solution faster in bilevel routing, and perform best among methods without response-model derivatives in performative reinforcement learning.

### [365] [Prediction Is Not a Sufficient Memory State](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13881)
*Robert Jenkinson Alvarez*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: A memory that reproduces every current prediction may still have forgotten how to learn from the next observation. We characterize this distinction for exact cumulative learning and attention. For smooth convex residual losses with unrestricted real features and labels, a continuous recurrent state of fixed dimension exists exactly when the loss is polynomial. With ordinary, unweighted observations, degree $D$ requires precisely $r=\binom{d+D}{D}-1$ coordinates; even among histories with one fixed current predictor, exactly $r-d$ coordinates can remain necessary for continuation. Nonpolynomial losses have unbounded requirements on such equal-prediction histories. Bounded scalar logistic examples retain this obstruction after fixing any finite derivative jet. For ridge regression, the hidden evidence is the design matrix: the exact state costs $dp+d(d+1)/2$, versus $dp$ for the predictor. On a well-conditioned zero-prediction family, optimal $B$-bit compression has average one-update error of order $d^{-1}2^{-2B/s_d}$, $s_d=d(d+1)/2$, even with arbitrary randomized codes. Kernel attention gives a second exact closure classification. The results identify what future updates reveal, rather than proposing a new regression algorithm or asserting trained-model gains.

### [366] [Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13917)
*Joseph Lee,Yanjing Li,Bo Qiang,Gregory Lau,Allyson Ettinger,Noah A. Smith,Rory Donovan-Maiye,David Baker,Hanna Hajishirzi,Pang Wei Koh*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: A central challenge in de novo protein design is generating proteins with desired structural and functional properties. Existing design models typically require a dedicated input representation for each property, limiting the design objectives they support. We develop Prompteina, the first all-atom structure generation model that supports new and broader design objectives specified in natural language, analogous to text-to-image generation. To train Prompteina, we construct Prompteina-Data, a paired text--protein structure dataset of 1.8M structures and 50M+ captions describing global and residue-specific structural and functional properties. We adapt Proteina-Complexa, a pretrained structure generation model, through text-conditioned pretraining and finetuning that aligns residues with their corresponding text. Prompteina outperforms baselines on 15 of 18 structural properties and generates proteins that more closely match descriptions of their intended functions. In binder design, it leads baselines on at least 13 of 20 targets and improves interface confidence by 14\% over the strongest baseline. With iterative in silico feedback, Prompteina's gain over non-iterative generation is 57\% larger than the next-best baseline on the hardest targets. Finally, we experimentally validate Prompteina designs against GM2A, a target with no reported de novo binders. We identify nine binders, with the strongest at an apparent $K_{\mathrm{D}}$ of 107 nM. These results establish natural language as an effective and powerful conditioning interface for protein structure generation.

### [367] [KL Before and After Mixing: A Round-Complexity Separation in Parallel Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13924)
*Tianyi Wu*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: A parallel sampler can choose at random which coordinates to generate together. For a target $p$ and the output law $q_U$ of a schedule $U$ drawn afresh for each output, we compare the schedule-averaged divergence $\mathbb{E}_U D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q_U)$ with the output-law divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|\mathbb{E}_U q_U)$, in nats. Rounds commit independent draws from exact conditional marginals frozen at the round's start, each output's schedule is drawn before sampling from a finite mixture of schedules, and every scheduled round is charged. For the uniform distribution on binary strings of even length $n$ with $n/2$ ones, the least expected number of rounds at a fixed tolerance $\varepsilon>0$ is $\Theta_\varepsilon((\log n)^2)$ under the first criterion but $(e^{-\varepsilon}+o(1))\log_2\ln n$ under the second, and the double-logarithmic order is attainable with the same round count on every run. For this target, a count-state recursion gives the exact least output divergence at every round cap over all causal randomized policies. The separation extends to weighted fixed-count targets with bounded weight ratios and quota fractions bounded away from zero and one, without permutation symmetry, and to the full-support Beta$(1,1)$--Bernoulli target, where the sharp expected cost under the output-law criterion is $(e^{-\varepsilon}/2+o(1))\log_2\log_2n$, attained with rare $n$-round runs. Prior work implies the order of the schedule-averaged cost on the balanced target and its $O_\varepsilon((\log n)^2)$ upper bounds on both extensions.

### [368] [AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13928)
*Andis Draguns,Sumeet Ramesh Motwani,Raymond Douglas,Christian Schroeder de Witt*

Main category: cs.LG

TL;DR: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training on a small chemical reaction prediction task - a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

### [369] [Ember: Making Unified Virtual Memory Practical for Discrete-Memory GPUs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13408)
*Senad-Leandro Lemes Galera,Michail Georgoulakis Misegiannis,Ferdinand Gruber,Jana Giceva,Dimitrios Stavrakakis*

Main category: cs.OS

TL;DR: Ember是一个用于离散GPU的UVM管理框架，通过默认映射到主机内存、按区域精细化管理数据位置，解决了GPU内存超额订阅时UVM性能崩溃的问题，在不需要应用修改或预剖析的情况下实现显著加速。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 随着GPU工作集快速增长（最大模型增~1000倍而GPU内存仅增~5倍），应用必须超额订阅GPU内存。NVIDIA UVM虽支持超额订阅，但一旦数据超过GPU内存，其基于缺页的放置策略会浪费互连带宽并导致严重的性能崩塌（如图1所示，GPU sort在1.5×超额订阅时从4.1s增至1150s）。现有方案要么手动编排数据放置（工作量大、与GPU世代耦合），要么借助profile-guided方法（不稳定、需额外运行），都无法透明支持未修改应用。论文提出核心研究问题：能否在无需placement hints、profiling运行或应用修改的前提下，让UVM超额订阅在现成GPU上变得实用？

Method: Ember引入"默认映射的混合地址空间"作为核心抽象，每条分配的每个region（VA block，2 MiB）在初始时均映射到主机内存，GPU可直接访问而无数据迁移。系统基于三个组件协同工作：(1) 迁移引擎负责混合地址空间，按region粒度执行提升/降级，提升时一次性迁移整个VA block并锁保护，避免小块迁移开销；(2) 访问监控器利用GPU硬件访问计数器（~256个仅覆盖host-resident内存的counter），将通知归因到对应VA block，并通过扩展邻接span（默认64 MiB）补偿counter数量不足的局限，将一个被访问块提升时一起提升其邻居；(3) 策略引擎实现两种策略——阈值提升在内存充裕时按counter阈值提升区域，避免超额订阅时立刻回收；基于衰减的积极回收在GPU占用率达上水位（90%）时按物理chunk执行批回收（每25 ms减半一次需求，按需求+迁移分数排序驱逐），至下水位（85%），并通过迁移感知保护（迁移分数+宽限期机制）防止区域抖动。提出两个实现：Ember-static为用户空间版（在stock CUDA上使用cudaMemAdvise+cudaMemPrefetchAsync固定划分，3个API调用/分配）；Ember-adaptive为内核模块版（打补丁到NVIDIA开源UVM驱动，按counter在线决策，无需修改应用）。使用GPU硬件counter的4 KiB页限制被绕过，并扩大其通知影响范围。

Result: 在三种部署场景的四张GPU（RTX 5080/A40/H200消费级+数据中心卡，以及GH200超芯片）上评估：数据密集型应用（pathfinder、k-means、CNN、双调排序、基数排序、BFS）方面，1.5×超额订阅时Ember-static较stock UVM几何均值加速6.83–10.62×，Ember-adaptive达5.52–8.83×，且性能增益随访问模式不规则性提升（顺序型1.8–10×，随机型11–225×）；LLM推理（Qwen2.5-14B、Qwen3-32B）方面，在16 GB封顶下超额订阅至1.41×时token生成4.7–16×加速（在手动放置根本无法加载模型的规模）；数据库分析（SSB on Crystal）Ember-adaptive在60组查询-GPU-容量组合的51组中获胜，对UVM加速1.50–2.36×；GH200上由于一致互连，UVM崩溃缓解，Ember加速回落至约3.5×但复用频繁的工作负载（k-means、LLM）仍显著优于UVM-mapped；与profile-guided方案HELM对比，Ember-adaptive无需profiling运行，在kernel时间上以2.1×几何均值领先（5个基准中3个胜出，bfs与gramschm因HELM契合而落后）；Ember-static在稳定热集频繁复用时更快，Ember-adaptive在低复用或单一pass场景下更快，两者在20 GB工作集/1.3×GPU内存下数据迁移量差异为静态版一次性16 GB迁移 vs. 自适应版6.8–65.2 GB。代码改动极少（<5% LOC）。

Conclusion: Ember证明了UVM超额订阅可在不改动硬件、内核或应用的前提下变得实用，通过将映射设为默认、按region粒度组织混合地址空间、利用GPU硬件访问计数器驱动运行时提升、并通过基于衰减的积极批回收保持驱逐远离关键路径。相比于以迁移为默认、映射为后备的方案，Ember将驱逐从超额订阅的固定开销变为可策略控制的决策，在广泛硬件（消费卡到GH200超芯片）和工作负载（数据密集型、LLM推理、数据库分析）上系统性地优于stock UVM、纯映射、预取和profile-guided方案。识别了Ember-adaptive在可观察性（仅知道counter，不能直接观测设备访问）、库内部缓冲区不可见、需要裸金属访问加载内核模块以及多GPU扩展等限制，但整体设计独立于CUDA，可迁移到其他支持驱动控制迁移与映射的栈（如AMD ROCm）。

Abstract: GPU working sets have outgrown GPU memory, so applications must oversubscribe it, keeping only hot data on the GPU. NVIDIA's Unified Virtual Memory (UVM) supports oversubscription, but its performance degrades once data exceeds the GPU's memory. This stems from its fault-driven data placement, wasting interconnect bandwidth, and underutilizing the GPU. This raises the question: can UVM oversubscription become practical on stock GPUs, exploiting GPU memory speed and minimizing wasted interconnect bandwidth, without placement hints, profiling runs, or application changes? To this end, we present Ember, a UVM management framework for oversubscribed workloads. Ember introduces a hybrid address space; allocations start as mapped into host memory, omitting data migration. Ember's counter-driven region promotion uses GPU's hardware counters to fetch hot regions to the GPU, its decay-based eager reclamation proactively evicts cold regions in batches, while via online region re-placement, Ember tracks the hot set at runtime. We implement Ember within NVIDIA's open-source UVM driver for unmodified applications and as a userspace variant on stock CUDA. At 1.5x oversubscription, it is 6.8-10.6x faster than UVM on six applications across three PCIe GPUs, and generates LLM tokens 4.7-16x faster at sizes where manual placement cannot run at all. Without a profiling run, it beats a profile-guided alternative by 2.1x on kernel time.

</details>


### [370] [PredictIO: Decoupling Workload Prediction from OS-Controlled Storage Prefetching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12971)
*Jun Lu,Yancan Mao,Zhenya Ma,Sheng Yue,Yongjian Fu,Ju Ren*

Main category: cs.OS

TL;DR: Storage stalls remain a significant source of application latency even on fast storage devices. Prefetching can hide part of this latency by fetching data before it is demanded, but general-purpose operating-system mechanisms typically infer future accesses from recent file offsets. This approach is ineffective when accesses are determined by workload structure, such as recurring sparse accesses during application launch, logical traversal in database scans, or model-layout metadata in LLM runtimes. Existing workload-aware prefetchers usually embed prediction logic inside individual applications and couple execution to application-level I/O paths, making policies difficult to reuse across workloads and systems. We present PredictIO, a programmable interface that separates workload prediction from prefetch execution. PredictIO delivers kernel-observed accesses and application hints to user-space policies, which express predictions as uniform page-range requests. A kernel-space executor validates, bounds, and filters these requests against cached and in-flight pages before issuing asynchronous prefetch I/O. We implement PredictIO for application launch, SQLite range scans, and LLM model loading. Across these workloads, PredictIO reduces latency by 5.3-26.3%, achieves up to 2.99x speedup for SQLite scans, and reduces LLM loading latency by 8.8-47.9%. We further show that a common prediction policy can be reused across SQLite and LMDB through lightweight adapters, that an application-integrated RocksDB readahead policy can be migrated while preserving its workload selectivity, and that the execution backend determines how much benefit migration provides for different access patterns and storage devices.

### [371] [Characterizing CPU-GPU Memory Sharing over Unified Memory Architecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13125)
*Jinrong Yang,Zimeng Wang,Rong Chen,Haibo Chen*

Main category: cs.OS

TL;DR: Unified Memory Architecture (UMA) enables the CPU and GPU to share a single physical memory. However, its complexity and opacity often drive applications back to inefficient copying or to incorrect direct access that sacrifices performance or even correctness. This paper presents a comprehensive study of CPU-GPU memory sharing on UMA, covering correctness and performance across data-plane transmission and control-plane coordination on four platforms. It yields four findings that guide libumsh, a portable library that delivers correct and efficient memory sharing across platforms and extends to emerging ones (e.g., NVIDIA DGX Spark). Applied to nine real-world systems, libumsh reduces data-plane time by 16-75% and control-plane overhead by 7-90%.
